title: PRD: Responsive sidebar + right-panel drawer behavior
description:
## Problem Statement

Under 1024px the three-panel layout breaks: the sidebar squeezes the chat, the right panel overlaps content. The mockups are desktop-only but we need to not break catastrophically on smaller screens.

## Solution

Below 1024px: sidebar collapses behind a hamburger button anchored top-left; opening it slides it over the chat as a drawer. Below 1024px: right panel becomes a bottom sheet with a "View document" toggle in the chat header. Above 1024px: behavior unchanged from PRD 4/6.

## User Stories

1. As a tablet user (768–1023px), I want a hamburger to access the sidebar.
2. As a tablet user, I want a "View document" button in the chat header that opens the document table as a bottom sheet.
3. As a phone user (<768px), I want the same drawer behavior but with the sheet covering ~90% viewport height.
4. As a user resizing the window across the 1024px breakpoint, I want the layout to adapt without losing my place or active chat.
5. As a developer, I want responsive behavior keyed off CSS only (no media-query React state) where possible to avoid hydration mismatches.

## Implementation Decisions

- Use Tailwind v4 `@media (max-width: 1023px)` utilities. Sidebar gets `lg:translate-x-0 -translate-x-full` (or equivalent) plus a backdrop. State managed by a UI store slice `responsiveStore` for drawer open/closed.
- Hamburger button is always rendered but `display: none` at `>=1024px`.
- Right panel below `lg` becomes a fixed bottom sheet (`position: fixed; bottom: 0; left: 0; right: 0;`) with its own open/close state.
- shadcn `Sheet` primitive may simplify both drawers — adopt if it fits.

## Testing Decisions

- Vitest is limited for media queries — we'll cover the toggle stores and a few snapshot tests at fixed sizes via `matchMedia` mocking.
- playwright-bdd at multiple viewport sizes (`viewport: { width, height }` per scenario): `responsive.feature` with scenarios for 600px and 900px viewports.

## Out of Scope

- Hand-polishing mobile typography or spacing.
- A separate mobile-first design pass.
- Touch gesture handling (swipe to open drawer).

## Further Notes

This is intentionally minimal — we want the desktop UX to feel right at all sizes without committing to a mobile design that may diverge later.
design:
Canonical mockups in `example-html/` (read the rule at `.claude/rules/frontend/ui-prototypes.md` first):

This epic touches every breakpoint — consult all three viewports:

**Desktop baseline (≥1024px)**: C, D (no changes from the desktop layout above the breakpoint).

**Mobile (<768px)**:
- **G — Empty state**: layout when no doc is pinned.
- **H — Doc pinned, mid conversation**: chat surface + how the right panel collapses.
- **I — Library bottom sheet**: doc picker as bottom sheet (target for `dj6` on mobile).
- **J — History drawer**: sidebar as slide-over drawer (target for `gbl` on mobile).

**Tablet (768–1023px)**:
- **L — Tablet, doc pinned**: hybrid layout — sidebar visible, right panel collapses.
- **M — Tablet, light**: light-theme tablet variant (cross-check with F).

Keep the responsive behaviour CSS-only where possible (Tailwind v4 `@media` utilities); only use a JS store for transitions that need explicit open/close state (sidebar drawer, right-panel sheet).

Workflow: open the files in a browser for the visual; grep for `--*` tokens and port to `design-tokens.css`. Never paste mockup HTML into the app.
notes:
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-14 by bqx.1)
- Drawer state is ephemeral (in-memory Store only, no localStorage). createResponsiveStore() factory pattern matches sidebarStore/themeStore but without persistence.
- Breakpoint reactivity uses window.matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)') with a change listener — NOT useMediaQuery-style React state, to keep CSS-only the dominant pattern (per epic decision "keyed off CSS where possible to avoid hydration mismatches").
- Grid template lives in .authed-grid (globals.css). CSS vars (--sb-w, --rp-w) flow in via inline style; @media query in CSS handles the column-template switch. Avoid Tailwind arbitrary grid-cols-[…] when commas are involved — CSS class + vars is cleaner.
- Modal/overlay surfaces wrap their content in <aside> with fixed positioning below lg + lg:relative above lg. Wrapper escapes the grid track below lg so the grid collapses to fewer columns naturally.
- Click-to-close backdrops should be <button aria-label='Close X'> not <div onClick> — keeps AT users on the happy path.
- Singleton stores leak state across vitest tests — add afterEach reset when tests mutate the singleton (see responsiveStore.test.ts:afterEach(closeSidebarDrawer)).
- All navigation handlers in _authed.tsx call closeSidebarDrawer() before navigate() so mobile users land cleanly. The store's closeSidebarDrawer is a no-op when already closed.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-14 by bqx.1)
- Drawer state is ephemeral (in-memory Store only, no localStorage). createResponsiveStore() factory pattern matches sidebarStore/themeStore but without persistence.
- Breakpoint reactivity uses window.matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)') with a change listener — NOT useMediaQuery-style React state, to keep CSS-only the dominant pattern (per epic decision "keyed off CSS where possible to avoid hydration mismatches").
- Grid template lives in .authed-grid (globals.css). CSS vars (--sb-w, --rp-w) flow in via inline style; @media query in CSS handles the column-template switch. Avoid Tailwind arbitrary grid-cols-[…] when commas are involved — CSS class + vars is cleaner.
- Modal/overlay surfaces wrap their content in <aside> with fixed positioning below lg + lg:relative above lg. Wrapper escapes the grid track below lg so the grid collapses to fewer columns naturally.
- Click-to-close backdrops should be <button aria-label='Close X'> not <div onClick> — keeps AT users on the happy path.
- Singleton stores leak state across vitest tests — add afterEach reset when tests mutate the singleton (see responsiveStore.test.ts:afterEach(closeSidebarDrawer)).
- All navigation handlers in _authed.tsx call closeSidebarDrawer() before navigate() so mobile users land cleanly. The store's closeSidebarDrawer is a no-op when already closed.

## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-14 by bqx.2)
- RightPanel is placement-agnostic: it accepts a className prop and an optional onClose. Parent decides column vs sheet chrome (border-l vs border-t, shadow, transitions). Component owns only its inner anatomy (header, body, copy-csv).
- Bottom-sheet pattern mirrors the drawer: fixed positioning below lg, lg:relative above lg, translate-y instead of translate-x. translate-y-full hides; translate-y-0 reveals.
- Auto-close on breakpoint crossing handles BOTH drawer and sheet via the same matchMedia listener — singleton stores must be reset when the viewport invalidates the mode.
- Stacked overlay anti-pattern: opening a Radix Dialog (e.g. DocPicker) while a fixed-positioned sheet is open produces two z-50 surfaces with overlapping focus. Always close the sheet first inside the handler.
- View document button (lg:hidden) is gated on documentId truthiness — never render a no-op affordance at mobile when there's nothing to view.
- Playwright .toBeVisible() reports translated-off-screen elements as visible (non-empty bounding box). Use data-attribute assertions (data-sheet="open|closed") for sheet/drawer open state, not visibility checks.
- .authed-grid drops to single-column below lg: 1fr only (no var(--rp-w) track). RightPanel lifts out via position: fixed at <lg, lg:relative joins the 3rd column at ≥lg.

title: PRD: Light theme toggle with system preference + persistence
description:
## Problem Statement

The frontend foundation defines both dark and light theme tokens, but there is no toggle and the dark theme is hardcoded as the default. Users with `prefers-color-scheme: light` should see the light theme by default; everyone should be able to override.

## Solution

On first load, respect `prefers-color-scheme`. Once the user toggles via UserMenu, the choice persists in localStorage and overrides the system pref. An inline script in `index.html` sets `<html data-theme>` before React hydrates to avoid theme flash. TanStack Store holds the active theme; the UserMenu shows a toggle (or three-state: system / light / dark).

## User Stories

1. As a user with system light mode, I want the app to render in light theme on first load.
2. As a user with system dark mode, I want the app to render in dark theme on first load.
3. As a user, I want to override the theme via the UserMenu.
4. As a user, I want my choice to persist across reloads.
5. As a user, I want to revert to "system" if I changed my mind.
6. As a user, I want no theme flash on initial paint.

## Implementation Decisions

- Theme store `src/theme/themeStore.ts`: `mode: 'system' | 'light' | 'dark'`. Effective theme = mode === 'system' ? matchMedia query : mode.
- Inline blocking script in `index.html` reads `localStorage['theme.mode']` (or default 'system'), resolves to a concrete theme, and sets `<html data-theme="...">` before any CSS or JS runs. Prevents flash.
- UserMenu shows a sub-menu "Theme" with three radio items: System / Light / Dark.
- Subscribe to `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)')` events so toggling system preference in OS updates the app immediately while in 'system' mode.

## Testing Decisions

- Vitest: theme store transitions correctly between modes; localStorage write/read.
- Vitest: inline script logic extracted into a function and unit-tested for each initial state.
- playwright-bdd: `theme.feature` — system pref light → renders light; manual switch to dark → persists across reload; switch back to system → reflects system pref.

## Out of Scope

- Per-page or per-component theme overrides.
- High-contrast or print stylesheets.
- Animated transition between themes.

## Further Notes

CSS variables are already defined in `globals.css` from PRD 2. Switching themes is purely a `[data-theme]` attribute change; no component code references theme directly.

title: PRD: Stop button + stream error UI
description:
## Problem Statement

Streams can be long. Users need to interrupt them. Also: streams can fail (network drop, server error, 409 concurrent same-conversation, 500). Right now those failures crash silently or render nothing.

## Solution

Add a Stop button to the composer area that appears while `useChat({ status }) === 'streaming'`. Clicking it calls `useChat`'s `stop()` and the partial assistant message is preserved with a "stopped" badge. Surface errors as an inline banner inside the chat thread with a "retry" affordance that re-sends the last user message.

## User Stories

1. As a user mid-stream, I want a visible Stop button.
2. As a user, I want clicking Stop to halt within ~1 second and preserve the partial response.
3. As a user whose stream errored, I want a clear inline banner telling me what failed.
4. As a user, I want a "Retry" button on the error banner that re-sends the message.
5. As a user, I want a 409 conflict (concurrent same-conv request) to show a tailored message ("another response is in progress"); retry waits for the in-progress stream to finish.
6. As a user, I want the input composer re-enabled after Stop so I can immediately type the next message.

## Implementation Decisions

- StopButton component renders inside the composer area; appears when `status === 'streaming' || status === 'submitted'`.
- Stopped assistant messages get a small chip badge ("stopped"). Implementation: track a Set<messageId> of locally-stopped ids in component state, render the badge for those.
- Error banner: `components/StreamErrorBanner.tsx` consumes the `error` value returned from `useChat`. Maps error → friendly copy: 409 → "Another response is in progress", 5xx → "Server error", network → "Connection lost". Banner is dismissable.
- Retry: re-invokes `sendMessage` with the most recent user message that had no successful assistant reply. For 409, retry is delayed until query polling shows no in-flight conversation.
- AI SDK 5 `onError` hook surfaces the error; we also listen for an `error` frame from the stream itself.

## Testing Decisions

- Vitest: StopButton renders only during streaming; click invokes stop callback.
- Vitest: StreamErrorBanner maps each error class to the right copy.
- Vitest: retry resends the last user message.
- playwright-bdd: `stop-and-recover.feature` — start a stream, click Stop, see partial + badge; trigger a 409 via a fake adapter; assert banner copy; click Retry; second stream completes.

## Out of Scope

- Auto-retry on network failure (intentionally avoided — streams aren't idempotent server-side).
- Diff between partial and full responses.
- Backend changes — the 409 is already emitted; we just render it.

## Further Notes

We won't auto-retry transient errors because backend conversations may already have committed the user message. Retry must be user-initiated.

notes:
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-14)
- **Playwright streaming SSE mock**: Playwright route.fulfill cannot stream chunked response bodies. For tests that need to hold an SSE stream open (e.g. exercise Stop / cancellation mid-stream), use page.addInitScript to monkey-patch globalThis.fetch in the browser. Return a Response wrapping a ReadableStream with a controller you keep, listen to init?.signal abort to close the stream. Canonical example: frontend/tests/e2e/steps/stop-and-recover.steps.ts.
- **Tag-scoped Before hooks**: playwright-bdd Before hook supports { tags: '@my-tag' } filter. Use it whenever a Before installs invasive global state (fetch override, addInitScript) that would shadow unrelated feature files. Pair with @tag on the feature file.

title: PRD: Sidebar chat history — list + resume conversations
description:
## Problem Statement

After sending the first message in PRD 7, the conversation id appears in the URL but reloading the page doesn't restore the chat. The sidebar shows no real conversations. The backend persists conversations + messages but has no read endpoints.

## Solution

Backend: two new read endpoints. `GET /v1/chats` returns the user's conversations joined with their pinned document for sidebar grouping. `GET /v1/chats/{id}/messages` returns the ordered message list. Both require `X-User-Id`. Both follow hexagonal layering.

Frontend: the Sidebar's chat list groups by document (collapsible doc sections, ticker + year on the header, conversation rows show first-user-message preview + timestamp). Clicking a row sets `?chatId=<id>&pinnedDocId=<doc_id>` and `useChat`'s `initialMessages` is seeded from the messages query. Stream completion invalidates `['chats']` so the sidebar refreshes.

## User Stories

1. As a returning user, I want to see all my prior conversations in the sidebar.
2. As a returning user, I want conversations grouped by their pinned document.
3. As a returning user, I want to click a conversation and have it open with the full message history.
4. As a returning user, I want the right panel to re-pin the conversation's document automatically.
5. As a returning user, I want to refresh the page and have the active chat persist.
6. As a returning user, I want the sidebar's filter input to live-search across conversation titles.
7. As a returning user, I want recently-active conversations sorted to the top within each document group.
8. As a user, I want a new conversation I just sent to appear in the sidebar within a beat (optimistic or via cache invalidation).

## Implementation Decisions

- Backend endpoint contract:
  - `GET /v1/chats` → `{ items: [{ id, document: {id, ticker, year, title}, last_message_preview, last_message_at }] }`, sorted by `last_message_at desc` server-side. (No pagination for now — typical user count is small.)
  - `GET /v1/chats/{id}/messages` → `{ items: [{id, role, content, created_at}] }`, ordered by `created_at asc`. 404 if conversation not owned by `X-User-Id`.
- Hexagonal layering: new `application/use_cases/list_chats.py`, `get_chat_messages.py`. Reuse existing conversation repo, extend with the join.
- Frontend: `lib/queries/chats.ts` exposes `useChatList()` and `useChatMessages(chatId)`. `useChat({ initialMessages: ... })` seeds from the messages query when present.
- Sidebar grouping: client-side `Map<documentId, Conversation[]>` built from the list. Doc header shows ticker + year. Filter input narrows by case-insensitive substring across `last_message_preview`.
- `last_message_preview` is the first 80 chars of the most recent user message (computed server-side via SQL).
- TanStack Virtual wraps the flat row list when grouped count exceeds a threshold.

## Testing Decisions

- Backend integration: seed two conversations, two docs, then `GET /v1/chats` returns the right groups + ordering. `GET /v1/chats/{id}/messages` returns messages in order. Cross-user access returns 404.
- Backend unit: ordering / preview calculation in the repo's joined query.
- Frontend unit: groupByDocument transform is a pure function with unit tests.
- Frontend component: sidebar renders grouped conversations, click navigates with both URL params.
- playwright-bdd: `resume-chat.feature` — send a message (PRD 7), reload page, conversation appears in sidebar, click it, message history re-renders, right panel re-pins doc.

## Out of Scope

- Renaming or deleting conversations.
- Pinning conversations to the top.
- Search across the message body (not just preview).
- Pagination of the chat list.

## Further Notes

`last_message_preview` is denormalized as a SQL expression — no schema column needed unless query cost becomes a problem.

title: PRD: Send message + stream end-to-end
description:
## Problem Statement

The whole point of the app is to chat about the pinned document. The user has a doc pinned but cannot yet send a message. Backend already streams SSE in Vercel-AI-SDK-v5 frame format — we need to (a) thread `document_id` through conversation creation in the backend, (b) wire the composer + message list + streaming hook in the frontend.

## Solution

Backend: schema migration adds `conversations.document_id NOT NULL` with FK to `documents.id`. `POST /v1/chat` and `POST /v1/chat/stream` accept `document_id` in the body when no `conversation_id` is provided; when `conversation_id` IS provided, the document is loaded from the conversation row. The system prompt template incorporates the document's pre_text, table, and post_text.

Frontend: composer at the bottom of the main column (TanStack Form, auto-growing textarea, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to send, disabled when no doc pinned). On send, append a user message optimistically and start streaming via `@ai-sdk/react`'s `useChat` with a `DefaultChatTransport` pointing at `/v1/chat/stream`. The transport's headers callback injects `X-User-Id` from `useAuth()`. Messages render via react-markdown + remark-gfm. On `onFinish`, invalidate the chat-list query so the sidebar refreshes.

## User Stories

1. As a user with a pinned doc, I want to type a question and press Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to send it.
2. As a user, I want my message to appear immediately in the chat thread, before the assistant responds.
3. As a user, I want to see the assistant's response stream in token-by-token.
4. As a user, I want a pulsing cursor / typing indicator in the assistant bubble until the first token arrives.
5. As a user, I want a new conversation to be created when I send my first message with a pinned doc.
6. As a user, I want the conversation id to appear in the URL after the first turn so I can share or bookmark.
7. As a user, I want assistant messages to render basic markdown (bold, italic, lists, tables, code blocks).
8. As a user with no doc pinned, I want the composer disabled with a tooltip "Pin a document first".
9. As a user near the character limit, I want a counter at >28k characters (limit is 32k).

## Implementation Decisions

- Schema: `conversations.document_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES documents(id)`. The table is currently effectively empty (no users) — safe to ship as NOT NULL immediately.
- Use case: `start_chat` (current path) now requires `document_id` when `conversation_id` is None; raises `ValueError` otherwise. The use case fetches the doc, builds a system prompt with the doc payload, and emits the stream.
- API contract: `POST /v1/chat[/stream]` body becomes `{message, conversation_id?, document_id?}`. Validation: `document_id` required iff `conversation_id` is absent.
- System prompt template lives in `application/prompts/system_prompt.py`. Includes a short framing + the doc's pre_text + table (JSON) + post_text. Token budget: cap pre_text and post_text at 8KB each (truncate from the middle if needed) to leave plenty of headroom for multi-turn.
- Frontend: `lib/transport/createChatTransport.ts` returns a configured `DefaultChatTransport` with dynamic headers and `prepareSendMessagesRequest` to shape the body (includes `document_id` on first turn, `conversation_id` thereafter).
- Composer: TanStack Form, `textarea` with `field-sizing: content`-style auto-grow shim, key handler for Cmd/Ctrl+Enter. Character count appears at >28k. Send button disabled when value is empty OR when no pinned doc.
- MessageList: virtualized via TanStack Virtual once we have many messages, but trivially scrollable in this slice.
- MessageBubble: user (right-aligned) vs assistant (left-aligned), assistant uses react-markdown + remark-gfm. Pulsing cursor renders inside the bubble until first `text-delta`.

## Testing Decisions

- Backend integration: `POST /v1/chat/stream` with `document_id` and no `conversation_id` creates a conversation, returns the conversation id in the `data-conversation` frame, persists user message + assistant message. Stream completes with `[DONE]`. Without `document_id` AND without `conversation_id` → 400.
- Backend unit: system_prompt template renders correctly with realistic doc shapes.
- Frontend unit: `createChatTransport` builds the right body on first turn vs subsequent turns.
- Frontend component: Composer renders, Cmd+Enter triggers send when not empty + doc pinned, disabled state shows tooltip.
- Frontend component: MessageBubble renders markdown (bold + list).
- playwright-bdd: `send-and-stream.feature` — pin doc, type message, press Cmd+Enter, see optimistic user message + pulsing assistant bubble + streamed tokens + final URL contains `?chatId=`.

## Out of Scope

- Stop button (PRD 9).
- Error UI (PRD 9).
- Chat history list rendering real data (PRD 8).
- Resume an existing chat (PRD 8).
- Reasoning trace / citations rendering (later epic).

## Further Notes

The system prompt's exact wording is intentionally simple in this slice — we just need the assistant to be aware of the pinned doc. Prompt-engineering for accuracy is its own deliverable, deferred.
notes:
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-11)

- **System prompt = framing + doc payload**: settings.system_prompt is framing only; the per-turn prompt is built by application/prompts/system_prompt.py from the conversation's document. Don't reintroduce a static prompt.
- **One async-generator use case**: SendMessageUseCase.stream(user_id, conversation_id, user_text, document_id=None). Sync presenter consumes it and assembles a snapshot; streaming presenter emits SSE. Never add a parallel `complete()`.
- **DocumentRepository.get returns None for missing** — the use case maps None to DocumentNotFoundError. Don't make the adapter raise.
- **conftest seed fixture**: `seeded_document_id` (and the DB-level seed in the `engine` fixture) gives every integration test a valid doc id without ceremony. Use it for any new chat test.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-11)
- **vitest 4 + RTL needs explicit cleanup**: src/test/setup.ts has `afterEach(() => cleanup())`. Without it (and without test.globals=true in vitest.config), multi-render component tests in one file leak DOM and getByRole sees duplicate matches. Don't remove this hook.
- **Disabled-reason hints, not tooltips**: when a control is disabled for a known reason, render the reason as a persistent visible `<span role=note>` linked via aria-describedby — not a hover-only Radix Tooltip. Tooltips are for transient affordances; disabled-reasons are documentation.
- **TanStack Form keyboard shortcuts**: `form.handleSubmit()` ignores value; guard `value.trim() === ''` inside `onSubmit` so Cmd+Enter on empty doesn't fire `onSend`. Plain Enter doesn't need an intercept — let the textarea's native newline behavior through and only catch `(metaKey || ctrlKey) && key === 'Enter'`.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-11)
- **Cursor logic = (in-flight && index === lastAssistantIndex)**: both 'submitted' and 'streaming' count as in-flight so there's no gap between user sending and first token. Last-assistant-only check prevents prior bubbles lighting up on a new turn.
- **Markdown safety = react-markdown defaults**: no rehype-raw. Assistant text is untrusted; default sandbox is the contract.
- **Avoid nested aria-live**: don't put aria-live on a container list AND a status element inside. Aria-hidden the decorative element or scope live to a specific bubble.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-11)
- **Pathless _authed layout is created BEFORE the auth epic lands**: routes/_authed.tsx just renders <Outlet/> so children can sit at the spec'd path. Don't move /app to a flat route just because the auth gate is unimplemented — the file location is the auth seam.
- **Search params are validated at the route, not in the component**: validateSearch on createFileRoute parses {chatId?, documentId?} once. Inside the route component, use Route.useSearch() / Route.useNavigate() (not the standalone hooks with {from: ...}) — the standalone form's path-id inference doesn't recognize the trailing-slash route id and tsc -b breaks.
- **Test mocks drive scenarios via real surface area**: the route test mocks useConvfinqaChat with a fake that calls onData/onFinish from inside sendMessage. Tests then exercise user behaviour (type → Cmd+Enter → see bubble + URL + invalidation) instead of poking captured handlers. Single integrated test beats three implementation-detail tests.

title: PRD: Pin doc + render financial table
description:
## Problem Statement

Picking a doc sets `?pinnedDocId=<id>` in the URL but nothing renders. The right panel should show the document's table (the financial-statement data the chat will reason about) plus the pre/post narrative text. The user should also be able to resize / collapse the right panel.

## Solution

When `pinnedDocId` is present, the right panel renders three sections: a header with the document title + "Change document" button (re-opens picker), a TanStack Table view of the structured `table_data` field, and the pre/post text below. The panel is resizable (drag handle) and collapsible (icon button); width persists in TanStack Store. Long column headers wrap; numeric values are right-aligned in JetBrains Mono. A "Copy as CSV" button serializes the visible table.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to see the financial table of the pinned document on the right side of the screen.
2. As a user, I want long header strings (e.g. "Year ended June 30, 2009") to wrap or truncate gracefully.
3. As a user, I want the row labels (first column) to stay visible while I horizontally scroll wide tables.
4. As a user, I want numeric values to be right-aligned and rendered in a monospace font for readability.
5. As a user, I want to copy the table as CSV with one click.
6. As a user, I want to resize the right panel by dragging its left edge.
7. As a user, I want the panel's width to persist across reloads.
8. As a user, I want to click "Change document" to open the picker again.
9. As a user, I want to see the pre_text and post_text below the table for context.

## Implementation Decisions

- TanStack Query: `useDocument(id)` with `staleTime: Infinity` (full payload is immutable once fetched).
- `lib/transforms/tableToRowMajor.ts`: takes `{col: {row: value}}` → returns `{ columns: string[], rowLabels: string[], data: (number|null|string)[][] }`. Pure function, unit tested.
- TanStack Table headless API: column defs derived from the row-major shape, sticky first column via CSS (`position: sticky; left: 0; background: var(--bg-page);`).
- `components/DocTable.tsx` renders the table; `components/RightPanel.tsx` is the wrapper with header, table, narrative text, and copy-as-CSV.
- `components/ResizableSplit.tsx`: pointer-based resize handle with min/max constraints (240px – 60% of viewport). Double-click resets to default 480px. Width persisted in `useSidebarStore` sibling slice `panelWidthStore`.
- Sentence-case for "Change document"; opens the picker dialog from PRD 5 by setting an internal `pickerOpen` URL search param.

## Testing Decisions

- Vitest: `tableToRowMajor` unit tests against a few realistic shapes including the JKHY 2009 sample (mixed numeric/string cells, varied column counts).
- Vitest: DocTable renders headers + rows from a given row-major dataset; sticky-column CSS is asserted via `getComputedStyle`.
- Vitest: ResizableSplit pointer events drag the width; double-click resets.
- playwright-bdd: `pin-document.feature` — picks JKHY 2009 page-28-3, asserts the table row "net cash from operating activities" appears in the right panel; resizes the panel and reloads; "Copy as CSV" puts the right bytes on the clipboard.

## Out of Scope

- Citation overlays on cells (deferred — needs PRD that adds reasoning stream parts).
- Editing or annotating the table.
- Server-side CSV download.
- Rendering very wide tables differently (handled via overflow + sticky column).

## Further Notes

Real ConvFinQA tables have between ~3 and ~20 columns and rarely more than ~30 rows. We don't need virtualization for the table body — but if a doc surprises us, TanStack Virtual can be dropped in.
design:
Canonical mockups in `example-html/` (read the rule at `.claude/rules/frontend/ui-prototypes.md` first):

- **D — Document pinned, ready for follow-up** (desktop): the right-panel table layout, sticky-first-column behaviour, document header, Copy-as-CSV affordance placement.
- **E — Mid-stream / reasoning trace / cell-level citations** (desktop): citation chips on table cells — defines the cell→citation visual link that the right panel must support.
- **H — Doc pinned, mid conversation** (mobile): right panel as bottom sheet on mobile (`bqx` wires the actual responsive logic; this defines the target anatomy).
- **L — Tablet, doc pinned**: tablet variant of the same surface.

Workflow: open the files in a browser for the visual; grep for `--*` tokens and port to `design-tokens.css`. Never paste mockup HTML into the app.
notes:
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-13)
- CSV/TSV exports MUST neutralise formula-injection prefixes (=,+,-,@,\t,\r) on STRING cells/labels/headers; numeric cells stay raw so SUM formulas don't break. Canonical impl: frontend/src/lib/transforms/rowMajorToCsv.ts. Rule: .claude/rules/frontend/csv-injection.md.
- The 'smart composer' pattern: a Right{X}Panel-style component owns its useQuery + transform and passes a plain row-major projection to a presentational <Table>. Tests mock fetch at the Response layer, not at the query layer.

title: PRD: Document picker — backend documents schema + endpoints + frontend picker UI
description:
## Problem Statement

The ConvFinQA dataset (3,458 docs / 20 MB JSON) is the corpus the LLM reasons over. The frontend needs a snappy, searchable picker so users can pin a document to start a conversation. Today the dataset only lives on disk and the backend has no document endpoints — both halves need to be built.

## Solution

Backend: add a `documents` table (Postgres) with a generated `tsvector` for FTS, plus a btree on year. An idempotent seed script reads `data/convfinqa_dataset.json` and inserts rows. Two new GET endpoints: `/v1/documents` (paginated metadata + free-text + year-range search) and `/v1/documents/{id}` (full payload). Built via the hexagonal pattern — domain port + adapter + use case.

Frontend: a `DocPicker` modal/dialog opened from the EmptyState CTA and from a sidebar button. Search box debounced via TanStack Pacer. Year-range slider. Virtualized result list via TanStack Virtual. Click a result → URL gets `?pinnedDocId=<id>` (pin handling itself is PRD 6).

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to search across thousands of documents by ticker, title, or topic.
2. As a user, I want to narrow results by year range.
3. As a user, I want results to appear within ~100ms as I type.
4. As a user, I want to see at least the title, ticker, year, and page on each result row.
5. As a user, I want to paginate / infinite-scroll through results without UI lag.
6. As a developer, I want a stable JSON contract on `/v1/documents` so the picker can swap UIs without backend changes.
7. As an operator, I want a one-shot `make seed-docs` to (idempotently) load the dataset into Postgres.

## Implementation Decisions

- Schema: `documents(id text pk, ticker text, year int, page int, title text, pre_text text, post_text text, table_data jsonb, search_tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS to_tsvector('english', coalesce(title,'')||' '||coalesce(ticker,'')||' '||coalesce(pre_text,'')) STORED)`. Indexes: `gin(search_tsv)`, `btree(year)`, `btree(ticker, year)`.
- Title derivation at seed time: use the doc id's file slug + page number as a human-readable title.
- Ticker derivation: regex out of the doc id's `Single_<TICKER>/<year>/page_<n>.pdf-<chunk>` shape.
- Endpoint: `GET /v1/documents?q=&year_min=&year_max=&cursor=&limit=` returning `{ items: [{id, ticker, year, page, title}], next_cursor: string|null, total: int? }`. `q` is run through `plainto_tsquery('english', $1)` and matched against `search_tsv`. Pagination is keyset on `(rank DESC, id ASC)` to keep it stable as the table is seeded.
- Endpoint: `GET /v1/documents/{id}` returns the full row including `pre_text`, `post_text`, `table_data`.
- Hexagonal layering: `domain/ports/documents_port.py` (Protocol), `application/use_cases/list_documents.py` and `get_document.py`, `adapters/persistence/documents_repo.py` (SQLAlchemy async), `entrypoints/api/routes/documents.py` (FastAPI).
- Seeder: `backend/scripts/seed_documents.py`. Streams the JSON, batch-inserts with `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE`. Wired into `make seed-docs` and called automatically by `make up` after `alembic upgrade head`.
- Frontend: `lib/queries/documents.ts` exposes `useDocumentList({q, yearMin, yearMax})` returning an infinite query keyed on filters. `DocPicker.tsx` opens as a shadcn `Dialog`, has the search input (debounced 200ms via TanStack Pacer), year-range slider, and virtualized result list.

## Testing Decisions

- Backend integration test: seed a sample of 20 docs into the testcontainer, query `/v1/documents?q=jkhy` → see JKHY rows; query with year_min=2010 → filter applies; pagination via cursor reaches every row exactly once.
- Backend unit test: `list_documents` use case with a fake repo asserts the search and filter arguments are passed through.
- Frontend unit: `lib/queries/documents.ts` — given a mocked fetch, the query builds the right URL.
- Frontend component test: DocPicker renders, typing triggers a debounced refetch, clicking a result navigates with the URL param set.
- playwright-bdd: `pick-document.feature` — open picker, type 'JKHY', see at least one result, refine by year, click result, URL contains `?pinnedDocId=`.

## Out of Scope

- Pinning behavior past setting the URL param (PRD 6).
- Rendering the document table (PRD 6).
- User-uploaded documents.
- Editing or deleting documents.

## Further Notes

The seeder must be idempotent so the alembic migration can run it in CI/dev/prod without re-fetching. Batch size of 200 rows per INSERT is plenty given the corpus size. Keep `pre_text` length capped at a sensible truncation when feeding into the FTS column (full text in the row, but only the first 2KB in the index) — current plan uses the whole thing, revisit if FTS index grows too large.
design:
Canonical mockups in `example-html/` (read the rule at `.claude/rules/frontend/ui-prototypes.md` first):

- **D — Document pinned, ready for follow-up** (desktop): the post-pick state — confirms the picker's success outcome.

  - TanStack Query v5 requires `initialPageParam` (set to `null as string | null`); `getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.next_cursor` is correct because v5 treats null as "no more pages".
  - No X-User-Id header — /v1/documents is PUBLIC by design (per dj6.3 log).
- **Test gotcha**: `await result.current.fetchNextPage()` resolves when the queryFn promise settles, but React 19 + RQ may not commit the new page synchronously. Pattern: `await fetchNextPage()` then `waitFor(fetchMock toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2))` THEN `waitFor(data.pages.length === 2)`. The double waitFor avoids a 1000ms-boundary timeout.
- **Architectural decisions**: queryKey is `["documents", "list", { q, yearMin, yearMax }]` — RQ structural-hashes the filter object so reference identity doesn't matter. Dropped the decorative `as const` on the return after audit.
- **Notes for next iteration**: dj6.6 (DocPicker dialog + debounced search + year slider) unblocked. The dialog will: (a) install TanStack Pacer for debounce, (b) consume useDocumentList({q, yearMin, yearMax}), (c) virtualize the result list (consider @tanstack/react-virtual since fxn.4 also wants it), (d) on click set ?pinnedDocId=<id> via Route.useNavigate. Mockups: C (empty/CTA → opens picker), D (post-pick state), I (mobile bottom sheet — bqx will retrofit responsive). dj6.7 (Gherkin) depends on dj6.6.

title: PRD: Empty app shell + sidebar skeleton
description:
## Problem Statement

After signing in, the user lands on `/app`. With no chats and no document pinned, the user needs an unambiguous "what do I do next" UI. The three-panel layout (sidebar / chat / right-panel) is established here so subsequent slices just fill in cells.

## Solution

Render the authed app layout with: (a) a left sidebar containing "ConvFinQA" brand, a "New conversation" button, an (empty) chat list grouped by document, and a search input — all skeleton; (b) a main column with an empty-state hero "Pin a document to start chatting" and a CTA to open the (yet-to-be-built) doc picker; (c) the right panel hidden until a doc is pinned. The sidebar is collapsible, with state persisted via TanStack Store.

## User Stories

1. As an authed user, I want to see the three-panel layout when I visit /app.
2. As an authed user with no chats, I want a clear empty state telling me to pin a document.
3. As an authed user, I want a "New conversation" button visible at the top of the sidebar.
4. As an authed user, I want a search input in the sidebar (functionally inert this slice — wired in PRD 8).
5. As an authed user, I want to collapse the sidebar to a thin rail to reclaim space.
6. As an authed user, I want my sidebar collapse state to persist across reloads.
7. As an authed user, I want a UserMenu (bottom-left or top-right) with sign-out and theme-toggle (toggle wired in PRD 10).

## Implementation Decisions

- Layout route `src/routes/_authed/__root.tsx` with three CSS grid columns. Right column collapses to width 0 until `pinnedDocId` URL search param is set.
- Sidebar component is a stateless presenter that takes a grouped chat list (empty for now) plus callbacks. TanStack Virtual is wired but trivially small in this slice.
- TanStack Store slice `ui/sidebarStore.ts` for `collapsed` + width. localStorage persistence via the store's middleware.
- EmptyState renders inside the main column when there is no `chatId` URL param.
- UserMenu component placeholder with avatar (initials from `userId`) and dropdown — uses shadcn `DropdownMenu`.
- No data fetching this slice — Sidebar always passes `chats=[]`. The shape is locked so PRD 8 can swap in real data with zero component changes.

## Testing Decisions

- Vitest component tests for Sidebar (renders brand, button, empty state) and EmptyState.
- Vitest test for `useSidebarStore` (default collapsed=false, toggle, persist to localStorage).
- playwright-bdd scenarios: "Empty app shows empty state", "Sidebar collapses and stays collapsed after reload".

## Out of Scope

- Real chat list data (PRD 8).
- Doc picker open/close (PRD 5).
- Theme toggle wiring (PRD 10) — UserMenu has the placeholder slot only.
- Right panel content (PRD 6).

## Further Notes

Pixel target: mockup C (empty state, no doc pinned). All spacing, type sizes, and colors must come from the design tokens — no magic numbers.
design:
Canonical mockups in `example-html/` (read the rule at `.claude/rules/frontend/ui-prototypes.md` first):

- **C — Empty state, no doc pinned** (desktop): the three-panel grid, sidebar anatomy, empty-state hero, UserMenu placement. This is the primary reference for this slice.
- **G — Empty state** (mobile): mobile empty surface so the layout degrades cleanly under 768px.
- **J — History drawer** (mobile): sidebar anatomy when rendered as a slide-over drawer. Not wired in this slice (that's `bqx`), but the component shape should accommodate it.

Workflow: open the files in a browser for the visual; grep for `--*` tokens and port to `design-tokens.css`. Never paste mockup HTML into the app.

title: PRD: Sign-in stub + AuthProvider seam
description:
## Problem Statement

The mockups include sign-in and sign-up pages. Real Cognito + Google auth is explicitly out of scope for this session, but we still need (a) the visual sign-in flow and (b) a single seam so swapping in `react-oidc-context` later is a one-file change.

## Solution

Render `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` routes pixel-matching mockups A and B. Both "Sign in" and "Continue with Google" buttons write `auth.userId = "dev-user-<uuid>"` to localStorage and navigate to `/app`. A central `AuthProvider` exposes `useAuth()` returning `{ userId, signOut }`. A route guard on `/app/*` redirects to `/sign-in` if no userId in storage.

## User Stories

1. As a visitor, I want to land on the sign-in page if I am not authenticated.
2. As a visitor, I want to click "Sign in" with any credentials and land on `/app`.
3. As a visitor, I want to click "Continue with Google" and land on `/app` (visual stub only).
4. As an authenticated user, I want my user id to persist across page reloads.
5. As an authenticated user, I want a "sign out" affordance that clears the stored user id and returns me to `/sign-in`.
6. As a developer, I want a single `useAuth()` hook that the rest of the app consumes for `X-User-Id`.

## Implementation Decisions

- AuthProvider lives in `frontend/src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx` with React context. Internally reads/writes localStorage key `auth.userId`. On mount, hydrates from storage. Exposes `signIn()` (writes a fresh uuid prefixed `dev-user-`) and `signOut()` (clears the key).
- Route guard: a layout route `_authed.tsx` that calls `useAuth()`; if `userId` is null, it `redirect()`s to `/sign-in`.
- Form library: TanStack Form for the email/password inputs. No validation beyond non-empty (we are visual-only).
- AuthLayout (`_anonymous.tsx`) for the sign-in/sign-up shell — branded header, centered card.
- Future Cognito swap point: replace `AuthProvider` internals with `react-oidc-context`'s `useAuth()` re-exposed under the same shape. Consumers do not change.

## Testing Decisions

- Vitest: hook unit test for `useAuth()` (initial state from storage, signIn writes a uuid, signOut clears).

- Token storage or refresh.
- Cognito/Google credential validation.
- Password reset / email verification flows.

Mockups A and B are the design source of truth. Buttons must be sized and colored exactly to the tokens defined in m1-foundation's globals.css. Sign-up route can reuse the sign-in component with different copy and a footer link.

title: PRD: Frontend foundation — Vite + React + TanStack + tests + CI
description:
## Problem Statement

There is no frontend yet. We need a clean React+Vite+TypeScript SPA scaffold that subsequent vertical slices can build on, with the test harness and CI green from day one.

## Solution

Scaffold a new `frontend/` workspace using Vite 7 + React 19 + TypeScript. Install and configure: TanStack Router (file-based via Vite plugin), TanStack Query, Tailwind v4 with design-token CSS vars for both themes, shadcn/ui base config, Vitest + @testing-library/react, Playwright + playwright-bdd. Configure a Vite dev proxy for `/v1/*` to `http://localhost:8000`. Add `Makefile` targets and a GitHub Actions workflow with two new jobs: `frontend-unit` (always) and `frontend-e2e` (on frontend or backend changes).

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want `cd frontend && pnpm dev` to serve the app on `http://localhost:5173`.
2. As a developer, I want API requests under `/v1/*` to proxy to the FastAPI backend without CORS errors in dev.
3. As a developer, I want `pnpm exec vitest run` and `pnpm exec playwright test` to run from `frontend/`.
4. As a developer, I want `make frontend-test` and `make frontend-e2e` for parity with backend make targets.
5. As CI, I want the frontend unit job to run on every PR and the e2e job to run only on frontend/backend changes.
6. As a future contributor, I want the design tokens for the dark and light themes already defined as CSS vars in `globals.css`.

## Implementation Decisions

- Package manager: pnpm (>= 10.28). Supply-chain hardening (`minimumReleaseAge: 10080`, `blockExoticSubdeps: true`) lives in `frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml`. `packageManager` field in `package.json` pins the exact version so CI/corepack agree.
- Vite plugin set: `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `@tanstack/router-plugin/vite`, `tailwindcss/vite` (v4 plugin).
- TanStack Router file-based: routes live under `frontend/src/routes/`, generated tree in `frontend/src/routeTree.gen.ts`.
- Tailwind v4: CSS-first config via `@theme` block in `globals.css`. No `tailwind.config.js`.
- shadcn/ui: initialize `components.json` with a custom theme that references our CSS vars. Do NOT copy any components yet — that happens in later slices.
- Vitest: `jsdom` environment, `@testing-library/react`, co-located `*.test.tsx`.
- Playwright-bdd: `frontend/tests/e2e/features/*.feature` + step defs in `frontend/tests/e2e/steps/*.ts`. `pnpm exec bddgen` generates Playwright specs before each run.
- CI cache: pnpm store path (`pnpm store path`) keyed on `frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `~/.cache/ms-playwright`.
- A placeholder landing route at `/` that renders "ConvFinQA — coming online" so smoke tests have something to assert.

## Testing Decisions

- Smoke test (Vitest): renders the root route, asserts the placeholder string.
- Smoke test (playwright-bdd): one Gherkin scenario `Feature: App boots / Scenario: Root route renders` that visits `/` and sees the placeholder.
- CI: both must be green before merging the foundation PR. No skipped tests.

## Out of Scope

- Auth UI (PRD 3).
- App shell components (PRD 4).
- Any feature route — only the placeholder landing.
- shadcn component copy-ins (each slice copies what it needs).

## Further Notes

The Makefile targets `frontend-install`, `frontend-dev`, `frontend-test`, `frontend-e2e` are convenience aliases that `cd frontend && pnpm ...`. The CI workflow YAML uses `pnpm/action-setup@v4` (reads `packageManager` from `frontend/package.json`).
notes:
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-10)
- Frontend lives at repo-root `frontend/` (sibling of `backend/`). Package manager: pnpm (>= 10.28). Local install: `cd frontend && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- Supply-chain hardening lives in `frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml`: `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` (1-week release-age gate) and `blockExoticSubdeps: true` (refuses git/http/file: transitive deps). `packageManager` in `package.json` pins the exact pnpm version so corepack/CI agree.
- Strict TypeScript baseline in tsconfig.{app,node}.json: `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` + `noImplicitOverride` (on top of Vite scaffold's `noUnusedLocals/Parameters/erasableSyntaxOnly/noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`).
- Placeholder copy is "ConvFinQA — coming online" — keep this string so smoke tests in tasks 0hu.5 / 0hu.6 stay stable.
- Root `.dockerignore` excludes `frontend/`; if the SPA ever needs serving from the backend image, add a multi-stage build instead of removing the ignore.
- Scaffolded versions (May 2026): React 19.2 · TS 6.0 · Vite 8 · @vitejs/plugin-react 6 · ESLint 10 · typescript-eslint 8.59. Newer than PRD text; revisit if regression seen.
- Vite scaffold drops a `frontend/.gitignore` that already covers `node_modules`, `dist`, `dist-ssr`, `*.log`, `.vscode/*`. Add `routeTree.gen.ts` and `playwright-report/`/`test-results/` in later tasks.

## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-10, migration)
- Local pnpm rule (`.claude/rules/frontend/package-manager.md`) has NO `paths:` filter — always attaches in this repo. Use `pnpm`/`pnpm exec`/`pnpm dlx`; never `bun`/`bunx`/`npm`/`yarn`.
- `pnpm install` honours `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` (workspace YAML). Recently-published versions will be skipped in favour of the most recent version that is at least 1 week old. Expect pnpm output to list "X.Y.Z is available" for very fresh releases — that's the gate working, not an error.
- CI: use `pnpm/action-setup@v4` (it reads `packageManager` from `package.json`). Never `oven-sh/setup-bun` or `actions/setup-node` with npm caching. Cache the pnpm store via `pnpm store path` keyed on `frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml`.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-10, TanStack)
- TanStack Router/Query versions installed: react-router 1.169.1 · react-query 5.100.9 · react-router-devtools 1.166.13 · react-query-devtools 5.100.9 · router-plugin 1.167.32. Release-age gate (10080) downgraded fresh patches as expected (e.g. react-router 1.169.2 noted available).
- vite.config plugin order is load-bearing: tanstackRouter() MUST precede react(). Reverse = stale route tree / HMR weirdness.
- autoCodeSplitting: true splits every route's `component` into a separate chunk via `?tsr-split=component`. Test mounts and Playwright must await router-rendered DOM (`findByText`, not `getByText`), since the chunk loads asynchronously.
- Routes use createFileRoute() → `src/routes/__root.tsx` (with createRootRouteWithContext for QueryClient plumbing) + `src/routes/index.tsx` (placeholder). routeTree.gen.ts is generated by the plugin and is gitignored + eslint-ignored.
- main.tsx wires QueryClientProvider OUTSIDE RouterProvider. Router gets context { queryClient } so loaders can `useQueryClient()` without prop-drilling. Type registration via `declare module "@tanstack/react-router" { interface Register { router: typeof router } }`.
- Devtools (router + query) live in __root.tsx behind `import.meta.env.DEV`. Do NOT mount them in main.tsx — keeps the production bundle free of devtools code.
- ESLint: `react-refresh/only-export-components` is `off` for src/routes/**. The plugin's allowExportNames doesn't help because route components are referenced (not exported) — they trip the "localComponents" branch. TanStack's vite plugin already injects its own __TSR_REACT_REFRESH__ shim that makes Route hot-reload-safe.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-11, shadcn base)
- shadcn/ui base config landed in 0hu.4. components.json points `tailwind.css` → `src/styles/globals.css`, aliases `@/*` → `src/*`, baseColor `neutral` (token names match our orange palette so utilities use brand colors). `lib/utils.ts` exports `cn()` (clsx + tailwind-merge).
- BLOCKER for shadcn add: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages: [.]` triggers shadcn's monorepo gate. Workaround until 0hu.10 resolves: `mv pnpm-workspace.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml.bak; pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <component>; mv pnpm-workspace.yaml.bak pnpm-workspace.yaml`. `*.bak` is gitignored.
- Theming integration: globals.css has `@custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme="dark"], [data-theme="dark"] *));` — shadcn's `dark:` Tailwind variants fire when an ancestor (or self) has `data-theme="dark"`, NOT on `.dark` class or media query. `:where()` keeps zero specificity so component classes win.
- shadcn presets (radix-nova, etc.) want extras we don't use: `@fontsource-variable/geist` (we use Inter), `shadcn` package (its tailwind.css overrides our theme), `radix-ui` (only when a component imports Slot/etc.). Audit deps post-init and prune to: clsx, tailwind-merge, class-variance-authority, lucide-react, tw-animate-css.
- Vite proxy in vite.config.ts: `/v1`, `/healthz`, `/readyz` → http://localhost:8000 with `changeOrigin: true`. Shared `backendProxy` const. NOT just `/v1` because backend's health endpoints live at root (k8s convention) — see 0hu.11.
- TS 6 deprecates `baseUrl`. `paths: { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }` works without `baseUrl` and resolves relative to the tsconfig file. Both tsconfig.json (shadcn reads this) and tsconfig.app.json (tsc -b for src/) need it.
- ESLint `react-refresh/only-export-components: off` is now scoped to BOTH `src/routes/**` AND `src/components/ui/**`. shadcn components export Component + variants constant — same root cause as the route-component pattern.
- Tokens our globals.css does NOT define (yet): `--color-destructive`, `--color-destructive-foreground`, sidebar-* tokens, chart-N tokens. Add per-slice when the first component referencing them lands. shadcn components compile fine without them; the tokens just resolve to empty `var()`.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-11, shadcn unblock)
- frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml MUST NOT contain a 'packages:' key for the current single-package layout. Keep only 'minimumReleaseAge: 10080' + 'blockExoticSubdeps: true'. shadcn CLI v4.7 refuses every command if 'packages:' is present — even 'packages: [.]' trips its 'monorepo root' gate.
- 'pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <component>' works directly with no workaround. The mv-pnpm-workspace.yaml-aside dance from 0hu.4 is OBSOLETE — do not propagate it.
- Re-adding 'packages:' is only legitimate when the layout actually becomes multi-package (e.g. frontend/apps/web + frontend/packages/ui); then invoke shadcn with '-c apps/web'.

title: PRD: Backend reorg — src/ → backend/src/
description:
## Problem Statement

The repo started as a Python backend and has the Python source at `src/convfinqa/`. It has now evolved into a full-stack project; we need to add a sibling `frontend/` folder. The current layout makes the boundary ambiguous and clutters the project root.

## Solution

Move `src/convfinqa/` → `backend/src/convfinqa/`, move `scripts/` → `backend/scripts/`, move `alembic/` → `backend/alembic/`, move `tests/` → `backend/tests/`. Update every tool that hardcoded the old path. Imports stay rooted at `convfinqa.*` per the project imports rule — only the wheel package path in `pyproject.toml` changes.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want backend code under `backend/` so that the frontend can live under `frontend/` without naming collisions.
2. As a developer, I want `make sync && make test && make up` to keep working unchanged after the reorg.
3. As CI, I want the existing GitHub Actions workflow to keep passing after the move.
4. As a Docker builder, I want `docker build` to find the source at its new path.
5. As an Alembic user, I want `alembic upgrade head` to find migrations at the new path.

## Implementation Decisions

- Use `git mv` to preserve history on every file.
- `pyproject.toml`: change `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["src/convfinqa"]` → `["backend/src/convfinqa"]`. Move `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath`, `testpaths`, `[tool.ruff]` `src`/`include` accordingly.
- `Dockerfile`: update `COPY` paths from `src/` and `scripts/` to `backend/src/` and `backend/scripts/`.
- `alembic.ini`: update `script_location` from `alembic` to `backend/alembic`.
- `Makefile`: update any references to `src/`, `alembic/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`.
- `.github/workflows/*.yml`: update path filters and any `cd` / working-directory references.
- `docker-compose.yml`: update build context if it hardcodes paths.
- `docs/`: update path references where they appear.
- `.beads/`, `data/`, `example-html/`, `frontend/` (when created) stay at repo root.

## Testing Decisions

- Existing test suite (`make test`) must pass after the move with zero changes to test code.
- New integration sanity: a CI step that builds the Docker image and curls `/healthz`.
- No new unit tests needed — this is a pure reorganization.

## Out of Scope

- Frontend bootstrap (PRD 2).
- Any new feature work.
- Restructuring inside `backend/src/convfinqa/` itself.

## Further Notes

This PRD is ALL AFK. The agent loops over the child tasks; each is mechanical. Rollback = `git revert`.
notes:
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-10)
- After moving src/, ruff isort no longer auto-detects `convfinqa` as first-party. Fix: `[tool.ruff] src = ["backend/src", "backend/tests"]` in pyproject.toml.
- Conftest computes `PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` — relative-up-three from `backend/tests/conftest.py` lands at repo root, where `alembic.ini` lives.
- `alembic.ini` stays at repo root with `script_location = %(here)s/backend/alembic`. `%(here)s` resolves to wherever alembic.ini sits, so the override is robust to the file moving later.
- Dockerfile COPY pattern: `COPY backend/src/ ./backend/src/` (preserve repo layout in image) — entrypoint reads `alembic.ini` from `/app/` and resolves `%(here)s/backend/alembic` accordingly.
- `backend/scripts/ralph/` must be in BOTH `.gitignore` AND `.dockerignore` (local Ralph state, including secrets in `notify.env`).
- Multi-task reorg PRDs: bundle into one atomic commit. Reference each closed task in the commit body for granular history.
