title: Slice 3: docker-compose app service + AWS creds flow + docs update
description:
## Parent PRD

convfinqa-s3m

## What to build

Wire the Dockerfile from Slice 2 into `docker-compose.yml` as a new `app` service alongside the existing `postgres` service, add the AWS credentials handoff (`make aws-creds` → `.aws.env` → compose `env_file`), add `make up` / `make down`, and update `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/how-to-run-the-app.md` to reference the new make targets.

End-to-end behaviour delivered:

- `make aws-creds` materialises STS credentials from the developer's SSO session into `.aws.env`.
- `make up` builds and starts the full stack; the `app` container waits for Postgres healthcheck, applies migrations, then serves `/health` 200.
- `make down` stops and removes the stack.
- `.aws.env` is gitignored.
- Documentation reflects the new commands.

## How to build it

### 1. `docker-compose.yml` — add `app` service

Append to the existing compose file (Postgres service unchanged, image stays pinned at `postgres:18.3-bookworm` per `.claude/rules/python/pyproject.md`):

```yaml
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    container_name: convfinqa-app
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    env_file:
      - path: .aws.env
        required: false
    environment:
      API_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://convfinqa:convfinqa@postgres:5432/convfinqa
      LLM_MODEL: ${LLM_MODEL:-bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0}
      AWS_REGION: ${AWS_REGION:-eu-west-2}
```

Notes on the contract:

- `env_file.required: false` so `docker compose up` does not error when `.aws.env` does not exist (e.g. first-time clone before `make aws-creds` runs). When the file is missing, AWS calls will fail at runtime with a clear boto3 error — the developer then runs `make aws-creds`.
- The DB hostname is `postgres` (compose service name), NOT `localhost`. The host-side `make run` workflow continues to use `localhost:5432` via the developer's `.env`.
- `API_HOST: 0.0.0.0` overrides `Settings.api_host` default of `127.0.0.1` so external mappings work. The host workflow keeps the safer loopback.
- Do not duplicate values that live in `Settings` defaults unless they MUST differ between host and container (only `API_HOST` and `DATABASE_URL` qualify).

### 2. `.gitignore`

Append:

```
.aws.env
```

Confirm `.env` and `.env.*` are already covered (today `.env.example` is committed and `.env` is gitignored — verify before merge).

### 3. `makefiles/docker.mk`

If Slice 1 punted this file, create it now:

```makefile
.PHONY: up down aws-creds

up: ## Build and start the dockerised stack (Postgres + app)
	docker compose up -d --build

down: ## Stop and remove the dockerised stack
	docker compose down

aws-creds: ## Refresh STS credentials into .aws.env (uses AWS_PROFILE or sandbox-admin)
	aws configure export-credentials --profile $${AWS_PROFILE:-sandbox-admin} --format env-no-export > .aws.env
```

Notes:

- `$${AWS_PROFILE:-sandbox-admin}` — Make eats single `$`; doubled `$$` reaches the shell as a single `$`. The shell then evaluates `${AWS_PROFILE:-sandbox-admin}`.
- `aws configure export-credentials --format env-no-export` produces `KEY=value` lines (no `export` prefix) — exactly what `env_file` expects.
- Add to root `Makefile`: `include makefiles/docker.mk`.
- Do NOT auto-trigger `aws-creds` from `up` (per the EPIC discussion). Document the order in CLAUDE.md.

### 4. Documentation updates

`CLAUDE.md` — replace the Build & Test section block with:

```markdown
## Build & Test

```bash
make sync                              # Install deps via uv
docker compose up -d postgres          # OR: make up (full stack)
uv run alembic upgrade head            # Only when running the host workflow
make aws-creds                         # Refresh STS creds (only when using `make up`)
make run                               # Run the API on the host
make test                              # Run unit + integration tests
```

Full walkthrough (AWS login, env file, cURL verification, CLI REPL) lives in
[docs/how-to-run-the-app.md](./docs/how-to-run-the-app.md).
```

`docs/how-to-run-the-app.md` — for each section, lead with the make target, then show the underlying command in a "what this runs" callout. Sections to update:

- AWS login → `make aws-creds` (with the `aws-login` and `switch-aws-env` prerequisites unchanged).
- Local Postgres → `make up` for full stack OR `docker compose up -d postgres` for host workflow.
- Migrations → `uv run alembic upgrade head` (host only — `make up` runs migrations inside the container).
- API server → `make run` (host) or `make up` (container).
- cURL verification → unchanged commands, but reference the make targets.
- CLI REPL → `make cli ARGS="chat"`.

Constraints (all rules under `.claude/rules/`):

- No comments explaining WHAT in code or scripts.
- No `[project.scripts]` additions.
- No reading `SETTINGS` directly inside route handlers / use cases (this slice does not touch route code).
- Imports rooted at `convfinqa.*`.
- Variable naming: no leading underscores in module-level constants.
- No new pytest tests for compose / make targets — the existing manual smoke is sufficient per the PRD's testing decisions.

### 5. Manual verification (single end-to-end smoke)

Before marking the slice done:

1. Fresh checkout, no `.aws.env`.
2. `aws-login && switch-aws-env sandbox-admin && AWS_PROFILE=sandbox-admin aws sts get-caller-identity` — confirm SSO session live.
3. `make aws-creds` — file created, contains `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=...`.
4. `make up` — Postgres comes up healthy; app container builds, applies migrations, listens on 8000.
5. `curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/health` → 200 with the expected JSON.
6. `docker logs convfinqa-app | head -50` — verify alembic ran clean and uvicorn is bound to 0.0.0.0.
7. `make down` — both containers stop and are removed.
8. Repeat from step 4 to confirm idempotence (alembic upgrade head is a no-op on the already-migrated DB).

If any step fails, fix and re-verify. Do NOT merge with a known-broken compose flow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker-compose.yml` defines an `app` service with `build` pointing at the repo Dockerfile, `depends_on.postgres.condition: service_healthy`, the documented `environment` block, and `env_file: [{path: .aws.env, required: false}]`.
- [ ] Postgres service unchanged (still `postgres:18.3-bookworm`, same volumes, same healthcheck).
- [ ] `.aws.env` listed in `.gitignore`.
- [ ] `makefiles/docker.mk` exists with `up`, `down`, `aws-creds` targets, each with `## ` docstrings discoverable via `make help`.
- [ ] Root `Makefile` includes `makefiles/docker.mk`.
- [ ] `make aws-creds` writes a non-empty `.aws.env` containing `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` keys (verified manually with an active SSO session).
- [ ] `make up` brings the stack up; `curl http://localhost:8000/health` returns 200 within ~30s.
- [ ] `make down` stops and removes both containers.
- [ ] App container logs show alembic upgrade head running before uvicorn (verified via `docker logs convfinqa-app`).
- [ ] App container runs as UID 1000 (verified via `docker exec convfinqa-app id`).
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` Build & Test section references `make sync`, `make up`, `make run`, `make test`, `make aws-creds`.
- [ ] `docs/how-to-run-the-app.md` updated to lead each step with the make target.
- [ ] `.aws.env` is NOT committed (verified with `git status` after running `make aws-creds`).
- [ ] No automated pytest tests of compose / Dockerfile added (per PRD testing decisions).
- [ ] Re-running `make up` against a stack that is already migrated does not error (idempotence verified).

## Blocked by

Slice 2 (Dockerfile must exist before compose can `build:` against it).

## User stories addressed

User stories 13, 14, 15, 16, 19, 21 from `convfinqa-s3m`.

title: Slice 2: Production Dockerfile + entrypoint + .dockerignore
description:
## Parent PRD

convfinqa-s3m

## What to build

A multi-stage `Dockerfile` at the repo root that produces a runtime-agnostic production image, plus a `.dockerignore` and a small entrypoint script. The image runs as non-root, applies alembic migrations on start, then `exec`s uvicorn so signals reach the server directly.

End-to-end behaviour delivered:

- `docker build -t convfinqa:local .` produces an image (≤ ~300MB target, single arch matching host).
- `docker run --rm -e DATABASE_URL=... -e API_HOST=0.0.0.0 -p 8000:8000 convfinqa:local` boots and applies migrations, then starts uvicorn on port 8000.
- The image runs as a non-root user (UID 1000, name `convfinqa`).
- The build context is small (no `.venv`, `.git`, caches, tests, `data/`, `.env*`, `.aws.env`).

## How to build it

### 1. `Dockerfile` (multi-stage)

**Stage 1 — builder**:

```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim AS builder

ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never

WORKDIR /app

COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project

COPY src/ ./src/
COPY alembic/ ./alembic/
COPY alembic.ini ./alembic.ini
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev
```

The two-step `uv sync` is intentional: the first call caches the dependency layer (changes to `src/` do not invalidate it). The second call installs the project itself.

**Stage 2 — runtime**:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm

RUN useradd --system --create-home --uid 1000 convfinqa

WORKDIR /app

COPY --from=builder --chown=convfinqa:convfinqa /app /app
COPY --chown=convfinqa:convfinqa scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh /app/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /app/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh

ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH" \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

USER convfinqa
EXPOSE 8000

ENTRYPOINT ["/app/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh"]
```

Constraints:

- Pin to `python:3.13-slim-bookworm` to align with `.python-version` (3.13.7) and `.claude/rules/python/pyproject.md` (bookworm preferred).
- Do NOT use `latest`, `alpine`, `trixie`, or bare `3.13`. Same reasoning as the Postgres pin in the project rules.
- Do NOT add a `HEALTHCHECK` directive in the Dockerfile — the compose file owns healthchecks (Slice 3). Keeps the image runtime-agnostic.
- Do NOT bake any AWS credentials, env files, or settings overrides into the image.
- Do NOT register a new `[project.scripts]` entry per `.claude/rules/python/pyproject.md`. The image uses the existing `convfinqa` and `main` console scripts only via `uv run` if needed; the entrypoint calls `uvicorn` directly via the venv's PATH.

### 2. `scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

alembic upgrade head

exec uvicorn convfinqa.main:create_app --factory --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

Why `exec`: makes uvicorn PID 1 inside the container. Without `exec`, the bash process traps SIGTERM and uvicorn never gets the graceful-shutdown signal until the 10-second kill timer fires.

Why `set -euo pipefail`: strict failure semantics. If `alembic upgrade head` fails, the container exits non-zero immediately and orchestrators can restart or alert.

Why hard-code `--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` here rather than relying on `Settings`: the container's network contract is fixed (it always listens on 0.0.0.0:8000 and the orchestrator maps externally). Letting `Settings.api_host` default to `127.0.0.1` keeps the host workflow safer. This is the ONE place where the container deviates from `Settings`-driven config; document inline why.

Place the script at `scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh` alongside the existing `scripts/install-prek-hook.sh` and `scripts/ralph`. Make it executable (`git update-index --chmod=+x` if needed).

### 3. `.dockerignore`

```
.venv/
.pytest_cache/
.ruff_cache/
.mypy_cache/
__pycache__/
*.pyc
tests/
.git/
.github/
.beads/
data/
docs/
.env
.env.*
.aws.env
Makefile
makefiles/
README.md
LICENSE
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
.python-version
.pre-commit-config.yaml
```

Goal: keep build context under a few MB, and ensure no secrets (`.env`, `.aws.env`) or developer caches end up in image layers.

### 4. Local verification (manual)

This slice does NOT add automated tests of the Dockerfile per the PRD's testing decisions. Manual smoke before merge:

- `docker build -t convfinqa:local .` succeeds.
- `docker images convfinqa:local --format '{{.Size}}'` returns a reasonable size (target ≤ 350MB; if much larger, audit the build context).
- `docker run --rm convfinqa:local --help` is NOT meaningful (entrypoint is the script). Instead: `docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/bash convfinqa:local -c 'id'` prints `uid=1000(convfinqa) ...`.
- `docker history convfinqa:local` shows two stages and no copies of `.venv`, `.git`, `tests/`, or env files (use `docker history --no-trunc`).

Full end-to-end booting against Postgres lives in Slice 3.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Dockerfile` exists at repo root with two stages (`builder`, runtime).
- [ ] Builder uses `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim`.
- [ ] Runtime uses `python:3.13-slim-bookworm`.
- [ ] Final image runs as user `convfinqa` (UID 1000), not root.
- [ ] `docker build -t convfinqa:local .` succeeds on a clean checkout.
- [ ] `docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/bash convfinqa:local -c 'id'` prints `uid=1000`.
- [ ] `scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh` is executable, uses `set -euo pipefail`, runs `alembic upgrade head` then `exec uvicorn ...`.
- [ ] `.dockerignore` excludes `.venv`, `.git`, `tests/`, `.env*`, `.aws.env`, caches, docs, Makefile.
- [ ] No new `[project.scripts]` entries are added.
- [ ] No AWS credentials or `.env` content are present in any image layer (verify with `docker history --no-trunc`).
- [ ] `pyproject.toml`, `Settings`, `convfinqa.config`, and any application code are NOT modified by this slice.
- [ ] No comments in the Dockerfile or shell script explaining WHAT; brief WHY notes where non-obvious (e.g. why two `uv sync` calls, why `exec`).

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately, in parallel with Slice 1.

## User stories addressed

User stories 9, 10, 11, 12, 17, 18, 24 from `convfinqa-s3m`.

title: Slice 1: Makefile run/test targets + pytest marker scheme
description:
## Parent PRD

convfinqa-s3m

## What to build

Add a Makefile-driven developer interface for tests and runtime, plus a path-based pytest marker scheme that splits the suite cleanly into `unit` and `integration` with strict enforcement.

The end-to-end behaviour delivered by this slice:

- `make test-unit` runs only the fast in-process tests (zero Postgres testcontainer boots).
- `make test-integration` runs only the testcontainer-backed tests.
- `make test` runs unit then integration sequentially (fast failure on the cheap suite).
- `make run` starts the FastAPI server via the existing `serve_app` console script.
- `make cli ARGS="<subcommand>"` invokes the Typer CLI.
- `make help` lists every target with a one-line description.
- A new test landing in any `tests/<dir>/` that has no path mapping fails collection loudly.
- A misclassified marker (e.g. `pytest.mark.unti`) fails because of `--strict-markers`.

## How to build it

### 1. Register markers in `pyproject.toml`

Under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, add:

- `markers = ["unit: fast in-process tests", "integration: tests that boot a Postgres testcontainer or external service"]`
- Append `--strict-markers` to `addopts` (or create the key if absent).
- DO NOT touch `asyncio_mode`, `asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope`, `testpaths`, `pythonpath` — those are protected by `.claude/rules/python/tests.md`.

### 2. Auto-tag conftest

Modify (or create, if absent) `tests/conftest.py`. Add `pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items)`:

- Build a path-prefix map (relative to `tests/`):
  - `api/` → `integration`
  - `entrypoints/api/` → `integration`
  - `adapters/` → `integration` (rationale: hexagonal adapters typically need testcontainers)
  - `cli/` → `unit`
  - `entrypoints/cli/` → `unit`
  - `domain/` → `unit`
  - `application/` → `unit`
  - `fakes/` → `unit`
- For each item, derive the relative path from `item.path` (or `item.fspath`) and the project tests directory, find the longest matching prefix, and apply the corresponding marker if neither `unit` nor `integration` is already present.
- After tagging, walk the items once more; collect any nodeids that still have neither marker. If non-empty, raise `pytest.UsageError(f"Unmarked tests: {nodeids}. Add a path mapping in tests/conftest.py.")`.

Constraints:

- No comments explaining WHAT (per `.claude/rules/python/comments.md`). A short WHY comment on the strict assertion is acceptable.
- Use `from convfinqa.logging import get_logger` if logging is needed (probably not).
- No imports from `src.convfinqa.*` — root all imports at `convfinqa.*` per `.claude/rules/python/imports.md`.
- No leading underscores on module-level constants per `.claude/rules/python/variables.md`.

### 3. Conftest behaviour test

Add ONE test (`tests/test_conftest_markers.py` or similar) using pytest's built-in `pytester` fixture. The test creates a synthetic mini-suite with one test under an unmapped path and asserts collection fails with a `UsageError`. Justification: the auto-tag is non-trivial logic that, if broken, silently mis-classifies the entire suite. Per `.claude/rules/python/tests.md`, this is the only meaningful test of the marker mechanism — DO NOT add tests that assert "this file has the integration marker".

The test itself is `unit` (no testcontainer). Place it under `tests/` root and ensure the conftest path mapping covers `tests/test_*.py` at root → `unit` (or apply an explicit `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit`).

### 4. Audit existing files

Confirm path-based classification matches the actual suite at the time of merge:

- `tests/api/test_chat*.py` → `integration` (testcontainer Postgres) — confirmed at PRD time.
- `tests/cli/test_smoke.py` → `unit` (CliRunner only) — confirmed.
- Any new files added between PRD writing and slice merging must fit the mapping or get a new path mapping.

### 5. Makefile fragments

Create `makefiles/test.mk`, `makefiles/run.mk`, `makefiles/docker.mk`. Include them all from the root `Makefile` via `include makefiles/*.mk` (or explicit `include` lines).

`makefiles/test.mk`:

```makefile
.PHONY: test-unit test-integration test

test-unit: ## Run unit tests
	uv run pytest -m unit -q tests/

test-integration: ## Run integration tests (testcontainer Postgres)
	uv run pytest -m integration -q tests/

test: test-unit test-integration ## Run unit then integration tests
```

`makefiles/run.mk`:

```makefile
.PHONY: run cli

run: ## Run the FastAPI server (uv run main → serve_app)
	uv run main

cli: ## Run the Typer CLI; pass args via ARGS="..."
	uv run convfinqa $(ARGS)
```

`makefiles/docker.mk`: created in this slice with empty placeholder OR deferred to Slice 3. Recommendation: **defer to Slice 3** so this slice does not introduce unused Make targets.

Update root `Makefile` to `include makefiles/test.mk` and `include makefiles/run.mk` (alongside the existing `include makefiles/env.mk`). Confirm `make help` still lists every target — the existing `help` rule greps `## ` docstrings.

### 6. Documentation

Out of scope for this slice — Slice 3 owns the docs sweep. This slice only ships the targets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `make test-unit` passes locally, runs zero testcontainer boots (verifiable: no Docker socket activity, runtime ≪ 1s for current `tests/cli/test_smoke.py`).
- [ ] `make test-integration` runs all `tests/api/test_chat*.py` and only those.
- [ ] `make test` runs unit first, integration second; failure in unit aborts before integration starts.
- [ ] `make run` starts uvicorn on the configured port; equivalent to `uv run main` today.
- [ ] `make cli ARGS="--help"` prints the Typer help.
- [ ] `make cli` (no args) prints the Typer top-level help (Typer's default behaviour).
- [ ] `make help` lists `test-unit`, `test-integration`, `test`, `run`, `cli` alongside the existing `sync` and `install-hooks`.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` declares `unit` and `integration` markers and `--strict-markers` is active.
- [ ] `tests/conftest.py` auto-tags every test in current `tests/` based on the path mapping.
- [ ] Adding a fresh empty file at `tests/_unmapped/test_x.py` causes `pytest` collection to fail with a `UsageError` listing that nodeid (verified by the new conftest test using `pytester`).
- [ ] No tests of the form "assert this file has marker X" exist (per `.claude/rules/python/tests.md`).
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q tests/` (no marker filter) still runs the full suite.
- [ ] No new comments explaining WHAT; only WHY where genuinely needed.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

## User stories addressed

User stories 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 20, 22, 23, 25 from `convfinqa-s3m`.

title: EPIC: DX bundle — Makefile, Dockerfile, compose app service
description:
## Problem Statement

As a developer working on convfinqa, I have to type long, error-prone commands every time I run tests, start the API, or open the CLI. I copy-paste from `CLAUDE.md` or muscle-memory, and the canonical command for "run the unit tests" doesn't exist — `uv run pytest -q tests/` runs everything, including testcontainer-backed tests that need Docker. There is no `Dockerfile`, so I can't hand a colleague a single `docker compose up` command, the production deployment story is undefined, and the only docker-compose service today is Postgres. The Makefile exists but only carries `sync` and `install-hooks`.

The friction is small per command but compounds: it slows new contributors, gives me no fast feedback loop for unit tests, and means CI/prod infra cannot be designed yet because nothing produces a runnable container image.

## Solution

Ship a small, opinionated developer-experience (DX) bundle:

1. A `Makefile` with five everyday targets — `test-unit`, `test-integration`, `test`, `run`, `cli` — plus three compose helpers (`up`, `down`, `aws-creds`). Each is a thin wrapper over the canonical command.
2. A pytest-marker scheme that splits the suite cleanly into `unit` and `integration`, with auto-tagging by path inside `tests/conftest.py` and a strict collection-time assertion that no test is unmarked.
3. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` that produces a runtime-agnostic production image (uv builder → slim Python runtime, non-root user, alembic migrations on entrypoint).
4. A docker-compose `app` service wired in alongside the existing `postgres` service so `docker compose up --build -d` boots the full stack locally. Local AWS credentials flow via a generated `.aws.env` file (using `aws configure export-credentials`), refreshed by `make aws-creds`. The Dockerfile pulls credentials from the boto3 chain so future production runtimes (ECS Task Role, EKS Pod Identity, IAM Roles Anywhere) work without image changes.
5. Update `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/how-to-run-the-app.md` to use the new make targets as the canonical commands.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want a single `make test-unit` command that runs only the fast, in-process tests, so that I get sub-second feedback while iterating on domain logic.
2. As a developer, I want a single `make test-integration` command that runs only the testcontainer-backed tests, so that I can verify the database boundary without paying for the unit tests every time.
3. As a developer, I want `make test` to run unit tests first, then integration tests, so that the slow suite never starts if a fast test is already broken.
4. As a developer, I want `make run` to start the FastAPI server with one keystroke, so that I do not need to remember the uvicorn factory invocation.
5. As a developer, I want `make cli` to launch the Typer CLI with one keystroke, so that I can drop into the chat REPL or other commands instantly.
6. As a developer, I want every test to belong to either the unit or integration suite, so that the suite split cannot rot through neglect.
7. As a developer, I want unmarked tests to fail collection loudly, so that mistakes are caught at PR time rather than going silent.
8. As a developer, I want test markers applied automatically based on path, so that contributors do not have to remember to add a decorator.
9. As a developer, I want a `Dockerfile` at the repo root that builds a production-grade image, so that I can hand it to any container runtime later without rewriting it.
10. As a developer, I want the production image to run as a non-root user, so that the deployment posture meets baseline container security expectations.
11. As a developer, I want the image entrypoint to apply alembic migrations before starting uvicorn, so that `docker compose up` is a single self-contained boot.
12. As a developer, I want a `.dockerignore` that excludes `.venv`, caches, tests, git history, and credential files, so that the build context is small and no secrets are baked into image layers.
13. As a developer, I want a docker-compose `app` service that depends on the Postgres healthcheck, so that the API never starts before the database is ready.
14. As a developer, I want `make up` to build and start the whole stack and `make down` to stop it, so that the dockerised flow is symmetrical with the host flow.
15. As a developer using AWS SSO locally, I want `make aws-creds` to materialise short-lived STS credentials into a `.aws.env` file, so that the dockerised app can call Bedrock without me hand-mounting `~/.aws`.
16. As a developer, I want `.aws.env` listed in `.gitignore`, so that I cannot accidentally commit short-lived credentials.
17. As a security-conscious operator, I want zero long-lived credentials baked into the image or env files, so that a leaked image or env file cannot grant durable AWS access.
18. As a future production operator, I want the Dockerfile to read credentials from the boto3 chain, so that ECS Task Roles / EKS Pod Identity / IAM Roles Anywhere work without rebuilding the image.
19. As a developer, I want `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/how-to-run-the-app.md` to reference the new make targets, so that documentation does not drift away from reality.
20. As a contributor, I want `make help` to list every target with a one-line description, so that the build interface is self-documenting.
21. As a developer running the host workflow (`make run` against compose's Postgres), I want my fast iteration loop preserved, so that adopting Docker for prod-shape testing does not slow my day-to-day.
22. As a developer, I want path-based marker tagging to live in a single conftest, so that adding a new test directory only requires editing one file.
23. As a developer, I want the marker registry in `pyproject.toml` to use `--strict-markers`, so that typos like `pytest.mark.unti` fail loudly.
24. As a developer, I want migrations to be applied inside the container via the entrypoint, so that the host Python and the container Python never disagree about schema state.
25. As a developer, I want `make run` to keep using the existing `serve_app` console script, so that there is exactly one way to start the API and config (host, port, reload) stays controlled by `Settings`.

## Implementation Decisions

### Test markers (HOW)

- **Register markers** in `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`:
  - Add `markers = ["unit: fast in-process tests", "integration: tests that boot a Postgres testcontainer or external service"]`.
  - Add `--strict-markers` to `addopts` so unknown markers fail.
  - Keep existing `asyncio_mode = "auto"` and `asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"` per `.claude/rules/python/tests.md`.
- **Auto-tag by path** in `tests/conftest.py` using `pytest_collection_modifyitems(config, items)`:
  - Treat path prefixes `tests/api/`, `tests/entrypoints/api/`, `tests/adapters/` (when populated with testcontainer-backed adapters) as `integration`.
  - Treat `tests/cli/`, `tests/entrypoints/cli/`, `tests/domain/`, `tests/application/`, `tests/fakes/` as `unit`.
  - For each `Item`, if neither marker is already present, apply the path-derived one via `item.add_marker(pytest.mark.<name>)`.
- **Strict collection assertion**: after auto-tag, walk `items` once more; if any item has neither `unit` nor `integration` markers, raise `pytest.UsageError` listing the offending nodeids. This means a brand-new test directory with no path mapping fails fast at collection time.
- **No per-module `pytestmark`**: the auto-tag is the source of truth. If a single test must opt out, it can carry an explicit override marker — but this is the exception, not the rule.
- **Audit existing files** before merging: confirm every file in `tests/api/`, `tests/cli/`, etc. classifies correctly. The known files today are `tests/api/test_chat*.py` (integration — testcontainer Postgres) and `tests/cli/test_smoke.py` (unit — Typer `CliRunner` only).
- **No meaningless tests** per `.claude/rules/python/tests.md`: do NOT add a test that asserts "the marker was applied". The behaviour is verified implicitly by `make test-unit` / `make test-integration` running the right subset.

### Makefile layout (HOW)

- Keep the existing `Makefile` shape: `.DEFAULT_GOAL := help`, `SHELL := /bin/bash`, `include makefiles/*.mk`, `make help` greps for `## ` docstrings.
- Add new fragment `makefiles/test.mk` with: `test-unit`, `test-integration`, `test`. Each is one line wrapping `uv run pytest -m <marker> -q tests/` (or both for `test`).
- Add new fragment `makefiles/run.mk` with: `run`, `cli`. `run` shells out to `uv run main`. `cli` shells out to `uv run convfinqa $(ARGS)` so `make cli ARGS="chat"` works.
- Add new fragment `makefiles/docker.mk` with: `up`, `down`, `aws-creds`.
  - `up`: `docker compose up -d --build`.
  - `down`: `docker compose down`.
  - `aws-creds`: `aws configure export-credentials --profile $${AWS_PROFILE:-sandbox-admin} --format env-no-export > .aws.env`. Note the doubled `$$` because Make eats single `$`.
- Every target gets a `## ` description so `make help` lists it.
- Targets are `.PHONY` since none produce files.

### Dockerfile (HOW)

- **Two stages**:
  - Stage 1 (`builder`): `FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim AS builder`. Set `WORKDIR /app`. Copy `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` first, then `RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project` to cache the dep layer. Copy `src/`, `alembic/`, `alembic.ini`, then `RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev` to install the project.
  - Stage 2 (`runtime`): `FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm`. Create a non-root user (`useradd --system --create-home --uid 1000 convfinqa`). Copy `/app/.venv` and project files from `builder` with `--chown=convfinqa:convfinqa`. Set `PATH=/app/.venv/bin:$PATH`. Switch to the non-root user via `USER convfinqa`. `EXPOSE 8000`.
- **Entrypoint**: ship a small shell script `scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh` that runs `set -euo pipefail; alembic upgrade head; exec uvicorn convfinqa.main:create_app --factory --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`. `ENTRYPOINT ["scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh"]`. The `exec` is critical so uvicorn becomes PID 1 and receives signals correctly.
- **API host override**: the container sets `API_HOST=0.0.0.0` either via the entrypoint script or compose env. The host loopback (`127.0.0.1`) default in `Settings` stays untouched so `make run` keeps the safer host binding.
- **No SETTINGS leak**: the entrypoint and Dockerfile MUST NOT hard-code values that exist in `Settings`. Per `.claude/rules/python/dependency-injection.md`, anything that varies by environment is a `Settings` field, overridden via env var.
- **No alembic on host inside the image**: the image installs alembic via the dev/runtime split? `alembic` is in main `dependencies` already, so it ships in the prod venv. Confirm before merge.
- **`.dockerignore`** at repo root excludes: `.venv/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `tests/`, `.git/`, `.github/`, `data/`, `.env*`, `.aws.env`, `*.pyc`, `__pycache__/`, `docs/`, `Makefile`, `makefiles/`, `README.md`. Keeps build context small and prevents host caches/secrets from being baked into image layers.

### Docker-compose `app` service (HOW)

- Add a second service `app` to `docker-compose.yml`:
  - `build: { context: ., dockerfile: Dockerfile }`.
  - `container_name: convfinqa-app`.
  - `depends_on: { postgres: { condition: service_healthy } }`.
  - `ports: ["8000:8000"]`.
  - `env_file: [.aws.env]` — file is generated by `make aws-creds`.
  - `environment:`
    - `API_HOST: 0.0.0.0`
    - `DATABASE_URL: postgresql+asyncpg://convfinqa:convfinqa@postgres:5432/convfinqa` (note hostname is `postgres`, the compose service name)
    - `LLM_MODEL: ${LLM_MODEL:-bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0}`
    - `AWS_REGION: ${AWS_REGION:-eu-west-2}`
- Postgres service unchanged: image stays pinned at `postgres:18.3-bookworm` per `.claude/rules/python/pyproject.md`.
- `.aws.env` added to `.gitignore`. `.env` already ignored.

### AWS credentials flow (HOW)

- **Local dev**: developer runs `make aws-creds` once per SSO session. Output is `.aws.env` in repo root (gitignored). Compose loads it via `env_file`. Credentials expire with the SSO session (~1 hour) — refresh by re-running `make aws-creds`.
- **Why not mount `~/.aws`**: the research summary in the EPIC discussion confirms SSO-cached tokens reference host paths the container cannot resolve, so the boto3 SSO provider fails inside the container.
- **Why not bake creds into images**: violates the security goal in user story 17. `.dockerignore` blocks `.aws.env` from the build context; docker-compose injects it at runtime only.
- **Production**: not implemented in this EPIC. The Dockerfile is runtime-agnostic — boto3 picks credentials from env, container metadata service, or the EC2/ECS/EKS provider chain without any image change. A future EPIC will bind to a specific runtime (likely ECS Fargate + Task Role per the research).

### Documentation (HOW)

- Update `CLAUDE.md` "Build & Test" section: replace the four raw commands with `make sync`, `make up` (or `make run`), `make test`. Keep the link to `docs/how-to-run-the-app.md`.
- Update `docs/how-to-run-the-app.md` parallel sections for AWS login, env file, server start, cURL verification, CLI REPL — each step shows the `make` target first and the underlying command second (in a "what this runs" note) so the cheatsheet stays usable when Make is unavailable.
- Mention `make aws-creds` prominently as the prerequisite to `make up`.
- Do NOT add WHAT comments to the code or scripts per `.claude/rules/python/comments.md`. The Makefile `## ` strings are the exception (they ARE the help system, and they describe what — but `make help` is the user-facing surface, not code).

### Cross-cutting rules to honour (HOW)

- `convfinqa.*` import roots only — no `src.convfinqa.*`. Affects nothing in this EPIC since we do not write Python code outside `tests/conftest.py` (path-based marker logic uses `item.fspath` / `item.path`).
- No reading `SETTINGS` directly inside route handlers / use cases. The Dockerfile entrypoint sets env vars; `Settings()` reads them. Routes get `Settings` via the existing container — unchanged here.
- No new `[project.scripts]` entries. The two existing ones (`main`, `convfinqa`) are sufficient.
- Variable naming: no leading underscores in module-level constants. Affects shell scripts implicitly (use `AWS_PROFILE`, not `_AWS_PROFILE`).
- Logging: any new Python (only `tests/conftest.py` here) uses `from convfinqa.logging import get_logger` if it logs at all. `tests/conftest.py` does not need to log; `pytest.UsageError` carries the failure message.

## Testing Decisions

### What makes a good test for this EPIC

A good test verifies an externally-observable behaviour a user actually exercises. For this DX bundle, the user is the developer running `make ...`, and the relevant behaviours are:

- "When I run `make test-unit`, the testcontainer-backed tests do not run."
- "When I run `make test-integration`, all testcontainer tests run."
- "When a new test file lands in `tests/api/` without a marker, collection still classifies it as integration."
- "When a new test file lands in a directory with no path mapping, collection fails loudly."
- "When I `docker compose up --build -d`, the API answers `GET /health` with 200."

### What we will and will NOT test

- We will add **one** behaviour test for the conftest auto-tag: a `tests/conftest_test.py` (or `tests/test_conftest_markers.py`) that uses `pytest`'s `pytester` plugin to run a synthetic mini-suite with a deliberately unmarked test in an unmapped path and asserts collection fails. This is the only meaningful test of the marker mechanism and is justified because the auto-tag is non-trivial logic that, if broken, silently mis-classifies the entire suite.
- We will NOT add tests that assert "this file has the integration marker" — that is implementation detail per `.claude/rules/python/tests.md`.
- We will NOT add a pytest test that boots `docker compose up`. That would duplicate the existing testcontainer coverage and depend on Docker availability twice. The Dockerfile/compose are verified manually once during this EPIC (per the EPIC discussion) — `make aws-creds && make up && curl :8000/health` then `docker compose down`.
- We will NOT add a test that asserts `make run` invokes `serve_app`. Trivial wrapper, no logic.
- We will NOT add tests that assert imports work. Per `.claude/rules/python/tests.md`: "tests that check if we are able to import modules correctly … MUST be avoided at all costs."

### Prior art

- The auto-marker conftest test should follow the style of existing `tests/api/test_chat*.py` — minimal fixtures, behaviour-driven assertions, no monkey-patching. Use `pytest`'s built-in `pytester` fixture (no extra dependency).
- The async test infrastructure rules in `.claude/rules/python/tests.md` continue to apply: `asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"`, `loop_scope="session"` on `@pytest_asyncio.fixture`, async engines use `NullPool`, schema setup uses `alembic upgrade head` not `Base.metadata.create_all`. None of this changes here.

### Modules and what to test

- **`tests/conftest.py` (modified)** — single conftest test (as above) verifies auto-tag and strict-collection behaviour end-to-end.
- **`Makefile` + `makefiles/*.mk`** — no automated tests. `make help` is the contract; manual verification each target runs is sufficient.
- **`Dockerfile`** — no automated tests. Manual smoke per the EPIC discussion.
- **`docker-compose.yml` `app` service** — no automated tests. Manual smoke.
- **`scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh`** — no automated tests. The shell is trivial; `set -euo pipefail` plus `exec` is the entire logic. A bash unit test would be more code than the script.

## Out of Scope

- Selecting a production compute target (ECS Fargate, EKS, App Runner, Lambda). The Dockerfile is runtime-agnostic; the runtime decision becomes a separate EPIC.
- Terraform / CDK / IaC for any cloud resource.
- A CI workflow (GitHub Actions) that runs `make test` on PRs. Worthy follow-up; not bundled here.
- A `make migrate` target for the host workflow. Worth filing as a follow-up if the user wants it.
- Caching strategy for the Docker build inside CI (BuildKit cache mounts, registry cache).
- Hot-reload inside the container (the prod image runs without `--reload`).
- Linting / typecheck make targets (`make lint`, `make typecheck`). Pre-commit already runs them; `make check` aggregate is intentionally skipped.
- An automated container smoke test in pytest. Manual verification once during this EPIC instead.
- Multi-arch builds (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64). Single-arch matching the developer's host is fine.
- Image registry choice (ECR, GHCR, Docker Hub).

## Further Notes

- **Beads label**: every issue under this EPIC gets `milestone:dx-bundle` so autonomous agents can pick it up. The EPIC itself is also labelled `milestone:dx-bundle`.
- **Slicing**: three child issues, each independently mergeable. (1) Makefile + markers + conftest. (2) Dockerfile + entrypoint + .dockerignore. (3) Compose `app` service + `.aws.env` flow + docs update. The third issue depends on the second; the first is independent.
- **Unresolved questions remaining from the grilling phase**:
  - Whether to add a `make migrate` target for the host workflow. Default: no, file as follow-up.
  - Whether `make cli` should accept arguments via `make cli ARGS="..."`. Default: yes, as documented above.
  - Whether `make up` should auto-refresh `.aws.env`. Default: no, manual `make aws-creds` first.
  - Whether to force `API_RELOAD=true` in `make run`. Default: leave env-driven.
  - Whether `.env.example` should grow `API_HOST` / `API_RELOAD` examples. Default: yes — small change, improves discoverability.
  - Whether the auto-tag mapping for currently-empty `tests/adapters/` should default to `integration` (because adapters historically need testcontainers) or `unit`. Default: `integration` — it's the safer default given hexagonal adapter responsibilities.
- **Why no aggregate `make check`**: the user explicitly asked for "super super super simple". `pre-commit` covers lint/typecheck on commit; CI will (in a future EPIC) call `make test`. Adding `make check` now is premature.
- **Why a non-root user in the image**: baseline container security hardening; required by Pod Security Standards "restricted" and equivalent ECS hardened patterns. Free to add now, painful to retrofit later.
- **Why `exec uvicorn` in the entrypoint**: makes uvicorn PID 1, so SIGTERM from `docker stop` reaches uvicorn directly and graceful shutdown works. Without `exec`, the shell traps the signal and uvicorn never sees it until the 10-second kill timer fires.
- **Future hardening**: when prod runtime is chosen, add a non-root `USER` directive that maps to a UID matching the runtime's expected security context (e.g. EKS restricted PSS), pin base image digests, add a `HEALTHCHECK` directive (currently provided by compose). These are explicitly out of scope here.
notes:
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-10)
- **Pytest marker policy lives in `tests/marker_policy.py`** as a small importable helper (`PATH_MARKERS`, `apply_path_markers`, `unmarked_node_ids`). The conftest hook in `tests/conftest.py` calls these. This shape lets the pytester behaviour test exercise the real logic via import (in-process `runpytest()`, not `runpytest_subprocess`).
- **Adding a new test directory** requires editing `tests/marker_policy.py:PATH_MARKERS` to map the new prefix → `unit` or `integration`. Forgetting to do so makes collection fail with `pytest.UsageError` listing the offending nodeids — fail-fast by design.
- **Single test file at tests/ root** uses explicit `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit` rather than a root path mapping. If multiple root tests appear, prefer adding a root mapping then.
- **`pytest_plugins = ["pytester"]`** is loaded globally for the suite (top-level conftest requirement). Negligible cost; only relevant for tests using the `pytester` fixture.
- **`getattr(pytest.mark, name)` trips pyright strict** (`reportUnknownMemberType`). Branch explicitly: `pytest.mark.unit if name == "unit" else pytest.mark.integration`.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-10)
- **Hatchling reads README.md at install time**: `pyproject.toml` has `readme = "README.md"`. Any builder/installer step that does `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` (without `--no-install-project`) will fail with `OSError: Readme file does not exist: README.md` if README.md is excluded from the build context or not COPY'd into the image.  Either keep README.md out of `.dockerignore` and COPY it before the second `uv sync`, or use a no-readme strategy in pyproject (out of scope).
- **Two-step `uv sync` pattern**: First call `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project` after copying just `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` (cached dep layer). Second call `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` after copying `src/`, `alembic/`, `alembic.ini`, `README.md` (project-install layer, invalidates only on code/readme change).
- **Image runtime layout**: `/app/.venv` (deps), `/app/src` (code), `/app/alembic` + `/app/alembic.ini` (migrations), `/app/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh`. PATH starts with `/app/.venv/bin` so `uvicorn` and `alembic` resolve without `uv run`.
- **`useradd --system --create-home --uid 1000 convfinqa`** works on Debian even though `--system` typically picks UID < 1000 — explicit `--uid` overrides. The created GID is system-range (e.g. 999) which is fine.
- **`docker history --no-trunc` audit**: confirmed no `.git`, `tests/`, `.env*`, `.aws.env`, `.pytest_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `data/`, `.beads/` end up in any layer.
## Codebase Patterns (added 2026-05-10)
- **Compose `env_file` long form for optional files**: `env_file: [{path: .aws.env, required: false}]` is the compose v2.24+ syntax that lets a missing file be silently skipped. The shorter list-of-strings form (`env_file: [.aws.env]`) hard-fails when the file is absent — bad UX for a freshly-cloned repo.
- **`make aws-creds` syntax**: `aws configure export-credentials --profile $${AWS_PROFILE:-sandbox-admin} --format env-no-export > .aws.env`. Doubled `$$` so Make passes literal `${...}` to the shell. `env-no-export` produces bare `KEY=value` lines (no `export` prefix), exactly what compose `env_file` expects. Re-run when SSO session expires (~1 hour).
- **Health route is `/healthz`** (`src/convfinqa/entrypoints/api/health.py:6`). Don't write `/health` in docs/smoke tests.
- **Compose `app` service overrides only what differs from host**: `API_HOST=0.0.0.0` (vs `Settings.api_host=127.0.0.1` default) and `DATABASE_URL=...@postgres:5432/...` (vs `localhost`). Everything else inherits from `Settings` defaults / env. Don't duplicate values that match the defaults.
- **Compose's app uses container hostname `postgres`** (the compose service name), NOT `localhost`. Host workflow keeps `localhost:5432`. The two flows MUST stay independently runnable.

title: Concurrent-request 409 lock (pg advisory)
description:
## Parent PRD

Epic convfinqa-tvq

## What to build

Prevent two in-flight requests on the same conversation_id from interleaving via Postgres advisory lock with try-acquire semantics. If busy, return 409 application/problem+json with type https://convfinqa.local/problems/conversation-busy (sync) or domain ConcurrentRequest event mapped to 409 (stream).

Includes:
- In SendMessageUseCase.stream(), after persisting the user message and before the LLM call, open a transaction and call pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(conversation_id, 0)). On false -> yield ConcurrentRequest event.
- API maps ConcurrentRequest to 409 problem-details body in BOTH sync and stream presenters.
- The user message is persisted OUTSIDE this lock (its own transaction) so input is preserved even if a concurrent attempt is rejected.
- Test: two concurrent /v1/chat/stream requests against the same conversation_id; the first holds the LLM open via FakeLLMPort blocking primitive; the second returns 409.

## User stories addressed

(supports cross-cutting concurrency safety for stories 5, 6 — server-stateful integrity)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Two parallel POST /v1/chat/stream against the same conversation_id: second returns 409
- [ ] 409 body is application/problem+json with type=conversation-busy and status=409
- [ ] User message of the rejected attempt is NOT persisted (lock check happens after first user-msg persist of the holding request, but new arrival's user msg... clarify: per PRD, user msg persisted outside lock means each attempt's user msg lands; verify behavior matches PRD wording)
- [ ] Lock auto-releases on transaction commit/rollback (no leak on crash)
- [ ] Test simulates worker crash mid-lock and verifies next request succeeds

title: Enable ECS Exec + add psql to API image for sandbox DB inspection
description:
## Why
No interactive Aurora access from the operator's machine. CloudShell VPC environments don't work cleanly here — the no-NAT no-VPC-endpoints invariant blocks AWS API reachability from a CloudShell ENI in private subnets. ECS Exec into the already-running API task (public subnet, already has Aurora SG ingress, already has DATABASE_URL in env) is the smallest-friction option.

## Implementation

1. **TF — modules/compute/main.tf** on `aws_ecs_service.api`:
   ```hcl
   enable_execute_command = true
   ```

2. **TF — task role IAM** (the task ROLE, not the execution role):
   ```hcl
   data "aws_iam_policy_document" "ecs_exec" {
     statement {
       effect = "Allow"
       actions = [
         "ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel",
         "ssmmessages:CreateDataChannel",
         "ssmmessages:OpenControlChannel",
         "ssmmessages:OpenDataChannel",
       ]
       resources = ["*"]
     }
   }
   resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "ecs_exec" {
     role   = aws_iam_role.api_task.id
     policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.ecs_exec.json
   }
   ```

3. **Dockerfile runtime stage** — add `psql`:
   ```dockerfile
   RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends postgresql-client \
     && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
   ```

## Usage
```bash
AWS_PROFILE=sandbox-admin aws ecs list-tasks --cluster <c> --service-name <s>
AWS_PROFILE=sandbox-admin aws ecs execute-command --cluster <c> --task <t> \
  --container <name> --interactive --command /bin/bash
# inside:
psql "${DATABASE_URL/+asyncpg/}"
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `aws ecs execute-command` returns an interactive shell in the API container
- [ ] `psql "$DATABASE_URL_STRIPPED"` opens an interactive Postgres session against Aurora writer endpoint
- [ ] `\dt` lists the migrations + app tables

## Audit note
ECS Exec sessions are captured by CloudTrail by default. Skip `executeCommandConfiguration.logging` (terminal output capture) until there's more than one operator.

description:
## Parent

title: Persist sidebar collapsed-group state per user
description: SidebarChatList holds collapsedGroups as in-component state — refreshing the page resets all groups to open. Persist per user (likely via the same persistence layer being added in milestone:m3-persistence and the uf5 theme epic) so users keep their layout across reloads. Spec from fxn.4's PRD says 'open by default' which is the initial mount behavior — this ticket covers durability.

title: Extract financial number formatter from DocTable
description: DocTable inlines `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { maximumFractionDigits: 4 })`. The rounding policy is implicit and untested. When a future slice introduces decimal-heavy fixtures (ratios, percentages, currency with cents), extract a documented `formatFinancialNumber` util with unit tests for 2-decimal, 4-decimal, trailing-zero, and Infinity/NaN inputs. AC: existing DocTable tests still pass; new util replaces the inline call in DocTable.tsx.

value: Fresh AWS account ALB creation 403: GitHub deploy role lacks iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole. One-time bootstrap per account (NOT terraform-managed): `aws iam create-service-linked-role --aws-service-name elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com`. SLR is account-wide singleton; subsequent ALB creates use the existing role. Same pattern applies to other AWS service principals that auto-create SLRs (ECS, autoscaling, etc.) but ELB is the one we hit on convfinqa sandbox.

Playwright addInitScript fires on EVERY navigation including reload. Tests that simulate a localStorage change followed by reload need a NEW addInitScript call after the change (last-write-wins among addInitScripts) — page.evaluate alone is wiped on reload by any prior addInitScript that re-seeds the same key. Pattern used in convfinqa frontend/tests/e2e/steps/theme.steps.ts (uf5.4).

alembic migrations with generated tsvector columns: inline the to_tsvector(...) expression as a string constant DIRECTLY in the migration file. Do NOT import a shared constant from ORM models. Migrations must be frozen snapshots — if a shared constant changes later, fresh DBs get the new expression while already-migrated DBs keep the old, silently diverging. Keep the ORM constant separate for model use.

useModalDialog hook at frontend/src/lib/ui/useModalDialog.ts provides reusable modal a11y package (role=dialog/aria-modal toggled at usage site via spread to bypass Biome's useAriaPropsSupportedByRole false-positive on conditional aria-modal; Tab trap; Escape-to-close at container scope so Radix Dialog Esc still wins for nested portals; initial focus via data-modal-initial-focus opt-in with first-focusable fallback; restore focus to document.activeElement captured at open). Pair with useIsBelowLg() for the 1024px breakpoint trigger. The advisor's three concrete gotchas (jsdom offsetParent=null, lg:inline-flex hidden first focusable on mobile, container-scoped Esc to avoid stomping Radix) are baked into the hook.
AWS provider v6: data.aws_region.current.name is deprecated — use .id instead for the region string (e.g. eu-west-2)

Bedrock Claude Haiku 4.5 from London (eu-west-2): not in-region (only eu-north-1, eu-west-1 host directly), but eu-west-2 IS a valid SOURCE for the EU cross-region inference profile bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0. The 'global.' profile also accepts eu-west-2. Source: AWS Haiku 4.5 model card + inference-profile support matrix. Don't 'correct' eu-west-2 to eu-west-1 — both work, eu-west-2 keeps boto3 calls in London while CRIS routes the inference.

Files matching '.env' (including .env.example, .env.local, etc.) are blocked from Read AND Bash cat by ~/.claude/hooks/protect-files.sh and block-cat-sensitive.sh. Workarounds: 1) read committed content via 'git show HEAD:.env.example'; 2) ask the user to apply changes manually and surface the diff. Edit/Write tools also fail because they require Read first. Don't try to bypass — surface to the user.

Health endpoints: backend exposes /healthz and /readyz at root (k8s liveness/readiness convention, unversioned). /v1/* is reserved for app endpoints like chat. Frontend dev proxy (vite.config.ts) proxies /v1, /healthz, /readyz. PRD 0hu.4 criterion 2 originally said fetch('/v1/healthz'); amended 2026-05-11 (via convfinqa-0hu.11) to fetch('/healthz') because adding a versioned alias purely to satisfy a literal criterion is busywork and would muddle the convention. Do NOT add /v1/healthz to backend.

JS Object.keys + JSON.parse REORDER integer-like string keys: keys parseable as 32-bit unsigned int (e.g. '2007','2008') iterate FIRST in ascending numeric order, then non-integer keys in insertion order. The JKHY 2009 cash-flow doc table has columns 'Year ended June 30, 2009','2008','2007' on the wire; after JSON.parse they iterate as '2007','2008','Year ended June 30, 2009' — backwards for display. lib/transforms/tableToRowMajor.ts faithfully preserves whatever JS hands it (AC = 'preserves input dict insertion order'), but the wire order is lost upstream at JSON.parse. Follow-up: convfinqa-tha. Will bite convfinqa-9ye.2 (DocTable) when it first renders real data.

Cognito access tokens: no 'aud' claim, use 'client_id' claim instead. email field absent by default (only in ID tokens). Always validate token_use=='access' to reject ID tokens. Adapter in adapters/auth/cognito_jwks.py uses injectable fetch_jwks callable for testability.

convfinqa SETTINGS singleton anti-pattern: src/convfinqa/config.py:SETTINGS exists ONLY for the lifespan to bootstrap the container once. Inside route handlers, use cases, and adapters NEVER import SETTINGS — inject Settings via container/DI dependency (entrypoints/api/dependencies.py:SettingsDep). Reading SETTINGS directly defeats Container.for_testing(settings=...) overrides and breaks tests with custom configs. Caught in slice 1 quality gate.

FRONTEND PACKAGE MANAGER: ALWAYS pnpm, NEVER bun/npm/yarn. Pinned by /Users/francescoalbanese/Documents/Development/convfinqa/.claude/rules/frontend/package-manager.md. Supply-chain: minimumReleaseAge=10080 + blockExoticSubdeps=true in pnpm-workspace.yaml (or .npmrc equivalent). CI uses pnpm/action-setup@v4. The convfinqa-0hu epic was wrongly scaffolded with Bun on 2026-05-10; remediation tracked under convfinqa-0hu.9 (blocks all sibling .2-.8). Before adding any frontend dep or scaffolding ANY JS workspace, re-read this rule.

Pytest marker auto-tag pattern: extract the path→marker policy (PATH_MARKERS dict + apply/unmarked helpers) into tests/marker_policy.py rather than inlining in conftest. The conftest hook calls the helpers, AND the pytester behaviour test imports them and runs the real logic via runpytest() (in-process). Avoids duplicating the policy in a synthetic conftest. Use explicit branching (pytest.mark.unit if name == 'unit' else pytest.mark.integration), not getattr(pytest.mark, name) — the latter trips pyright strict reportUnknownMemberType.

Sidebar virtualization is deferred to convfinqa-fxn.4. gbl.2 ships Sidebar.tsx without @tanstack/react-virtual; the API contract is locked at SidebarChatGroup[] (id, documentId, documentTitle, chats[]) so fxn.4 can swap in the virtualizer without prop changes. Reason: AC for gbl.2 does not mention virtualization, fxn.4 explicitly owns 'grouped chat list + filter + Virtual', virtualizing [] is dead infra.

TTLCache[K, V] in strict pyright: cachetools TTLCache is invariant, so field declarations and __post_init__ assignments need # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType,reportAssignmentType,reportAttributeAccessIssue]. Keep ignores narrow, one code each.

Biome 2.x in convfinqa frontend (set up 2026-05-11 in 0hu.8): config at frontend/biome.json, lefthook.yml at REPO ROOT (not in frontend/ — lefthook walks to git root for discovery; frontend-scoping via glob:'frontend/**' + root:'frontend/'). Indent: tab + double quotes for TS/TSX (matches Vite scaffold), JSON gets space/2. CSS parser MUST have tailwindDirectives:true so globals.css with @custom-variant/@theme/@utility parses. Override 'useComponentExportOnlyModules: off' for src/routes/** + src/components/ui/** (Biome's react-refresh equivalent — same scope as the prior eslint config). Replaced eslint scripts with format/lint/check/ci/typecheck. 'biome ci' = read-only CI variant, 'biome check --write' = local autofix all-in-one.

Biome a11y rule useAriaPropsSupportedByRole false-positives on <aside role={x?'dialog':undefined} aria-modal={x?true:undefined}> because static analysis can't pair the conditional attrs. Workaround used in this repo: build the dialog attrs in an object (typed as Record<string, unknown>) and spread it onto the JSX element — Biome can't introspect spread keys. Pattern at frontend/src/routes/_authed.tsx + frontend/src/components/RightPanel.tsx.

Use Vercel `streamdown` for ALL assistant-message markdown rendering. NEVER `react-markdown` + `remark-gfm`. Streamdown is API-compatible with react-markdown's components prop but handles unterminated chunks during SSE streaming (no flicker on half-closed code fences/tables/bold), ships GFM by default, has prompt-injection hardening, and is from the same vendor as @ai-sdk/react which we depend on. Required CSS wiring in frontend/src/styles/globals.css: `@import "streamdown/styles.css";` and `@source "../../node_modules/streamdown/dist/*.js";`. For plain text bubbles use `controls={false}` to suppress code/table copy buttons until a ticket asks for them. See .claude/rules/frontend/markdown-streaming.md. Decision made in convfinqa-lzf after rb3.6 originally specced react-markdown.

Vitest fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers) break Radix Dialog + TanStack Query tests: rAF gets mocked too, so Radix focus traps and React 19 scheduling stall and tests time out at the default 5s. For debounce tests rendered inside a Dialog: use REAL timers + waitFor with a generous timeout (1000ms) to assert the debounced fetch URL. If you truly need fake timers for non-Radix surfaces, scope them via vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setTimeout','clearTimeout'] }) to leave rAF alone. Hit during convfinqa-dj6.6 (DocPicker).

lefthook pre-commit MUST chain vite build → pnpm test as one piped command, NOT run them as parallel siblings. @tanstack/router-plugin regenerates frontend/src/routeTree.gen.ts during every vite build, and vitest reading that file mid-write produces flaky empty <div/> renders in authedShell.test.tsx and app.test.tsx (router fails to register routes). Fixed in 2026-05-12 by collapsing build+test into a single 'build-and-test' command running 'pnpm exec vite build && pnpm test'. Rule documented in .claude/rules/frontend/quality-gates.md. Caught by convfinqa-1v3.

shadcn CLI v4.7 monorepo gate (resolved 2026-05-11 in convfinqa-0hu.10): frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml MUST NOT contain a 'packages:' key under the current single-package layout. Keep only 'minimumReleaseAge: 10080' + 'blockExoticSubdeps: true'. With that, 'pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <component>' works directly with no workaround. Re-add 'packages:' only if a true multi-package frontend workspace is introduced (e.g. apps/web + packages/ui); then invoke shadcn with '-c <subdir>'. Rule lives in .claude/rules/frontend/package-manager.md.

alembic revision strings must be 32 chars or less — alembic_version.version_num is VARCHAR(32). Symptom: StringDataRightTruncationError on alembic upgrade. Fix: shorten the revision string in the migration file (filename can differ). Confirmed in convfinqa-f7f.92.

asyncpg raw SQL pattern: use CAST(:param AS uuid) not :param::uuid — the :: cast syntax conflicts with asyncpg's SQLAlchemy parameter rendering and causes ProgrammingError. Always CAST when passing UUID strings in text() queries.

convfinqa streaming disconnect test pattern: httpx ASGITransport CANNOT mid-stream-disconnect (it runs the ASGI app to completion regardless of client.stream context exit). Solution: test the GeneratorExit handler at the use-case layer with await events.aclose(). This is sound because Starlette's StreamingResponse cancels by calling aclose() on the body iterator on real client disconnect — same code path. Don't try to make ASGITransport do mid-stream disconnect; spin up a real server only if you need end-to-end network behaviour.

GNU make exports command-line variable assignments into recipe shell env automatically (not just to sub-makes). Workflow trick `make … AWS_PROFILE=""` (intended to force the no-profile branch in our terraform.mk) ALSO leaks AWS_PROFILE="" into terraform's local-exec child shells. AWS CLI rejects empty AWS_PROFILE with `The config profile () could not be found`. Fix: `unset AWS_PROFILE` at top of any local-exec that calls aws CLI. See terraform/environmental/modules/keepalive/main.tf:111.

Playwright streaming SSE mock pattern: route.fulfill cannot stream chunked SSE bodies (body is buffered). To exercise mid-stream cancellation (Stop button, AbortSignal) in playwright-bdd, monkey-patch globalThis.fetch via page.addInitScript and return a Response wrapping a ReadableStream you control. Attach init?.signal abort listener to close the stream so useChat.stop() halts the mock. Tag-scope the install with { tags: '@your-tag' } so unrelated features aren't shadowed. Canonical example: frontend/tests/e2e/steps/stop-and-recover.steps.ts (convfinqa-bmu.4).

SQLAlchemy text() with PostgreSQL '::type' cast syntax (e.g. ':year_min::int') breaks parameter substitution under asyncpg — SQLAlchemy keeps the first :name unsubstituted (sees the trailing :: as part of the name) but substitutes subsequent occurrences, producing 'syntax error at or near :' from postgres. Fix: use CAST(:param AS type) instead. Hit on 2026-05-12 in convfinqa-dj6.2 documents_repo.py.

asyncpg + pytest-asyncio: 'cannot perform operation: another operation is in progress' on second test means a session-scoped async fixture is bound to a different event loop than the per-test loop. Fix: set asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope=session in pyproject [tool.pytest.ini_options] AND pass loop_scope='session' on every @pytest_asyncio.fixture AND use poolclass=NullPool on test engines. Verified in convfinqa slice 1.

convfinqa Postgres image pin rationale: docker-compose.yml uses postgres:18.3-bookworm. Don't change to: latest (moves with releases), bare 18.3 (default Debian base may flip), trixie (Debian 13, less mileage with asyncpg), alpine (musl, occasional asyncpg/locale edge cases). Bookworm = Debian 12, what testcontainers + most CI stacks use.

Node 25's globalThis.localStorage is an empty null-prototype stub (no setItem/clear/getItem etc) unless --localstorage-file is set. Vitest's populateGlobal skips it because it's not in its KEYS list, so jsdom's working Storage never reaches window.localStorage. Frontend tests need a manual in-memory Storage shim installed via Object.defineProperty in src/test/setup.ts. Rule documented at .claude/rules/frontend/test-localstorage.md.

Postgres partial index predicates must use IMMUTABLE functions only. now() and current_timestamp are STABLE, so WHERE expires_at > now() is invalid as a partial index predicate. Use a plain B-tree index on expires_at instead; the query WHERE clause handles the filter correctly at runtime.

convfinqa AWS stack design (May 2026): ECS Express Mode (Fargate + auto-wired ALB) for FastAPI streaming backend ~$28/mo. Aurora Serverless v2 Postgres min 0 ACU with keep-alive Lambda + SQLAlchemy pool tuning + frontend warmup loader. S3 + CloudFront OAC for SPA mirroring francescoalbanese-dev-infra pattern. Five TypeScript Lambdas (login/callback/refresh/logout/post-confirmation) for Cognito-with-Google auth setting HTTPOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax cookies. Single CloudFront domain app.convfinqa.francescoalbanese.dev with three behaviors: /api/v1/* → ALB, /api/auth/* → Lambda BFF, /* → S3. SSM Parameter Store SecureString for secrets. Postgres tables (not DynamoDB or Redis) for cache/rate-limit/idempotency via pg_cron TTL. Cognito sub mapped to users.cognito_sub UNIQUE in Postgres; row created by Post-Confirmation Lambda Trigger with defensive UPSERT in BFF callback as fallback. DNS records owned by convfinqa terraform via cross-account aws.shared_services provider into the parent francescoalbanese.dev zone in shared-services account. Single Terraform stack split into network/data/edge/compute/keepalive modules so terraform destroy -target=module.compute drops cost to ~$2/mo. One GitHub Actions workflow with path-filtered jobs; migrations as one-shot ECS RunTask before backend-deploy. Full rationale, runtime flows, disqualified alternatives, and operational runbook in docs/aws-architecture.html. Rule pointer at .claude/rules/infrastructure/aws-architecture.md.

convfinqa timestamp single-source-of-truth: when a use case persists a row with a created_at and the presenter needs that same timestamp in its response, the use case MUST surface it (e.g. via the Finish event). Calling datetime.now(UTC) in both the use case AND the presenter produces millisecond drift between the DB row and the HTTP body — flaky tests + inconsistent client UX. Caught in slice 1 quality gate.

Lefthook + beads coexistence (convfinqa, established 2026-05-11): beads owns core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks/. 'lefthook install' would conflict (--force overwrites bd shim, --reset-hooks-path unsets core.hooksPath). Solution: chain lefthook into .beads/hooks/pre-commit AFTER the BEADS INTEGRATION markers (file IS git-tracked, markers say external content preserved). frontend/scripts/install-hooks.sh re-applies idempotently via 'BEGIN LEFTHOOK CHAIN (frontend)' marker; wired as 'prepare' in frontend/package.json. Same approach applies if prek is ever activated for the backend.

user-event v14 click on Radix DropdownMenuRadioItem nested in a SubContent portal does NOT trigger onSelect/onValueChange under jsdom. Likely because the SubContent renders in a Portal and Radix uses pointer events the test runner doesn't dispatch through the portal correctly. PointerEventsCheckLevel.Never does not help. Fix: focus the radio element and use user.keyboard('{Enter}'). Both fireEvent.click(radio) and Enter work; keyboard is preferred (keeps test in user-event API, matches a11y flow). Pattern: radio.focus(); await user.keyboard('{Enter}'). Discovered in convfinqa-uf5.3 UserMenu theme submenu tests.
